Billionaire Lord’s Prestigious Italian Superyacht Is Asking for $27M
33 photos
Photo: TWW Yachts
“Andiamo” is a classy Italian name well-suited for an elegant superyacht built by one of the most prestigious shipyards in Italy. Although primarily known as the floating luxury toy of a billionaire English Lord, this yacht isn’t flashy and has managed to stayed away from media headlines and gossip; in fact, it could be simply described as pure balance.
One of the superyachts in the above-50-meter range that have recently joined the pre-loved yacht market doesn’t claim to be revolutionary or particularly striking. Its balanced look and overall qualities are what make it so appealing. You might even say that this isn’t the typical billionaire’s luxury toy, in the sense that there’s nothing sensational, outrageous, or immensely innovative about it. Still, it has all that it takes to be highly coveted.
Andiamo is not a new yacht, yet it had undergone a comprehensive refit recently enough to be considered “as good as new”. Most importantly, it carries the pedigree of one of the oldest and most reputable yacht builders in Europe, the famous Benetti, and that kind of heritage comes first even in comparison to a brand-new yacht in the same size, but from a lesser-known shipyard.
Andiamo was delivered in 2009 as Lady Lara. It is reported that it was originally built for a mining industry magnate from Kazakhstan, billionaire Alexander Machkevitch. The Italian yacht’s original name, Lady Lara, seems to have been inspired by the name of Machkevitch’s wife, Larissa. As we’ll see, Andiamo went from billionaire to billionaire, as one of the few “lucky” pleasure craft in this niche category to have only a couple of owners over decades.
Photo: TWW Yachts Usually, a superyacht that’s almost twenty-year-old would have a long list of former owners behind it, but that’s not the case with Andiamo. It changed hands once, going from Machkevitch to an unknown owner, and that’s when it was renamed Lady Luck. After that, it only changed hands again one more time, in 2017, when it was purchased by the one who is reportedly still its current owner after almost a decade – Sir Michael Hintze.
Lord Hintze was born in China to Russian parents, but was raised in Australia and eventually established himself in London, where the hedge-fund company he founded eventually made him a billionaire. He was knighted in 2013 for “services to the arts” (meaning hefty charitable contributions in this field) and later elevated to the House of Lords. Forbes currently ranks his fortune at $2.7 billion.
Almost a decade ago, when Lord Hintze allegedly purchased Lady Luck and renamed it Andiamo, the Italian yacht was listed at €35 million ($39 million today). Now, when the yacht has rejoined the market in search of a new owner, brokers claims that the current owner has spent more than €15 million ($16.7 million) in refits and upgrades over the years. That alone is an enormous sum, especially if you add it to the original selling price in 2017.
Still, it’s no secret that even the most luxurious yachts lose value relatively fast and that they cost their owners a lot of money in the end. Very few of these wealthy yacht owners, especially in the billionaire ranks, see these luxury toys as investments – they know they’ll pump more money into them than what they’re getting back (if anything), and it doesn’t stop them from buying an even more expensive yacht the next time.
Photo: TWW Yachts Andiamo’s most recent refit was completed relatively recently, in 2020, in Florida. The most striking and immediately recognizable change was its hull going from the standard white of many luxury yacht to a bold navy blue. The drastic paint job was part of a full exterior and interior revamping under the guidance of Patrick Knowles.
Refreshed and looking better than ever, this 17-year-old yacht has market appeal galore, starting with its undeniable Italian elegance. It combines a superyacht length of a little over 59 meters (195 feet) with 10.4-meter (34 feet) beam, a 3-meter (9.8 feet) draft, and a volume of just under 1000 GT (996 GT).
In short, this sums up as a yacht with considerable internal volume (perfect for comfortable accommodation) and access to smaller bays whether other yachts can’t reach, while the full-displacement hull design ensures greater stability for guests at anchor.
Andiamo’s elegant proportions and timeless style are owed to the original team that brought together Stefano Natucci for the exterior design, Benetti’s in-house team for naval architecture, and Studio Massari Interior Architecture and Design for the interior design, with all interior furnishings from the famous Italian Fendi brand. After the major 2020 refit, Andiamo’s interior and exterior carry the overlaying signature of Patrick Knowles.
Photo: TWW Yachts The generous six-stateroom layout can accommodate up to 12 guests, attended by a sizeable 15-person crew. The master suite takes center stage quite literally, spanning across two levels. This premium location makes room for a classic master’s office, a luxurious en-suite, and a modern observation lounge, in addition to the suite itself. Four guest cabins are located on the lower deck, while a VIP cabin and the Captain’s cabin are placed on the bridge deck.
Like any self-respecting luxury yacht, Andiamo pays great attention to outdoor living. The sun deck (everyone’s favorite place onboard) houses a large jacuzzi, plenty of sunbathing and lounging options, plus a contemporary-style outdoor gym. At water level, the transom turns into a spacious beach club with easy access to the water, as well as the garage that’s packed-full with water toys.
The new color palette clearly evokes a timeless maritime theme with bright blue and turquoise accents in conjunction with classic white – it matches the new hull paint color, and it makes Andiamo’s interior overall more visually striking. There’s also a bit of glam present, in the form of crystal, gold, and pearl accents, as well as high-quality marbles, woods, and lacquered finishes. Even the elevator that connects all decks is gold-plated for a more ornamental effect.
Performance-wise, Andiamo promises a cruising speed of 15 knots and a range of up to 6,000 nautical miles, powered by twin MTU engines. This means that Andiamo is just as good at transatlantic crossings as it is at accessing romantic little bays. Plus, recently-added zero-speed stabilizers ensure that the onboard experience is even more comfortable.
Photo: TWW Yachts It's also important to note that, although it has operated with great success on the luxury charter market in its past, Andiamo has taken a break from it over the past five years, during which it was enjoyed exclusively as a private pleasure craft. However, the yacht comes fully MLC-compliant and with low engine hours, which leaves it up to the next owner whether they will put this Italian beauty back on the charter market or not.
Andiamo’s current price tag is indicating €24 million ($26.9 million), which is not a lot, considering that it comes in great shape, fully refitted, and with overall investments valued at more than $15 million.
Above all, Andiamo comes from one of the most prestigious superyacht builders in Europe. Benetti has a long history spanning 150 years, and it’s the name behind several ultra-famous yachts, such as Spectre, Freedom, and Soundwave, all carrying the signature of iconic designers like Stefano Natucci and Giorgio Cassetta.

Ford Fathom EV pickup prototype (Source: Jim Farley)
Ford wants to make powering your home with an EV a lot cheaper. Its upcoming sub-$30,000 Fathom electric truck will feature a new bidirectional charging system that ditches the need for an expensive external inverter.
Arriving in 2027, the Fathom will be the first EV from a US automaker priced below $30,000 that can deliver more than 10 kW of AC power to a home without a separate wall-mounted inverter.
And Ford says it’s cutting the cost of the other equipment needed for home backup power, too.
How Ford’s cheaper bidirectional charging works
EV batteries store electricity as direct current (DC), but our homes use alternating current (AC). To send power from an EV battery into a house, traditionally, that meant installing a pricey external inverter.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Ford has come up with a different approach for its new Universal EV Platform, which will underpin the Fathom.
After acquiring startup Auto Motive Power in 2023, Ford redesigned its bidirectional charging system from the ground up. Instead of relying on a separate wall-mounted inverter, it built one directly into the truck’s E-box, one of the vehicle’s five main modules.
Fewer parts mean lower costs, and Ford says the savings will extend to the home charging equipment, too.
Fathom owners will have two ways to use the truck’s battery to power their homes.
Ford’s Home Power Station and Home Backup Panel. Photo: Ford
Home Power Management will let owners charge their truck when electricity rates are low, then use that stored power at home when rates are higher. That could mean real savings for households on time-of-use electricity plans. They’ll need Ford’s new Home Power Station, which the company expects to cost about half as much as its first-generation bidirectional charger.
Home Backup Power will let the truck keep the lights on during an outage. For that, owners will need both the Home Power Station and Ford’s Home Backup Panel. Ford says the backup hardware should cost at least 60% less than its first-generation equipment.
Ford hasn’t released prices for either piece of hardware, so we don’t yet know what a complete home installation will cost.
But pairing a sub-$30,000 electric truck with substantially cheaper home power equipment could make bidirectional charging a lot more appealing.
Ford is getting utilities involved early
Making the hardware cheaper is one thing. Making sure utilities can handle thousands of EVs that send electricity back into homes and potentially the grid is another.
Ford formed a working group in July with American Electric Power, BC Hydro, Consumers Energy, Exelon, and Pacific Gas and Electric. They’re working on making it easier for customers to connect bidirectional EVs before the Fathom arrives next year.
For example, someone using their truck solely for home backup power during an outage shouldn’t have to go through the same approval process as someone sending electricity to the grid.
The group is also looking at how to update utility procedures to accommodate newer bidirectional charging standards and make it easier for EV owners to participate in virtual power plants (VPPs). In other words, the batteries in parked EVs could become a useful source of electricity when the grid needs it most.
Ford says the Fathom’s system is designed to meet applicable UL 1741 requirements and IEEE 1547 interconnection standards. It also uses SAE J3068 communications technology, which Ford says helps reduce charger costs.
The idea is to get the technical requirements and utility processes sorted out before affordable bidirectional EVs start arriving in much larger numbers.
Electrek’s Take
Affordable EVs already offer some form of bidirectional power. Two of the cheapest electric cars in the US, the Chevy Bolt and Nissan Leaf, are both available for under $30,000.
The Bolt supports vehicle-to-home (V2H) power through GM Energy equipment, while the Leaf offers vehicle-to-load (V2L) capability through an external device plugged into its charging port.
Ford’s system takes things much further. It can deliver more than 10 kW of AC power to a home without an expensive external inverter, and Ford says the rest of the equipment will cost considerably less, too.
That’s a pretty compelling proposition, especially for people who live in areas prone to power outages or have electricity plans with higher peak-hour rates.

There are still some unknowns. Ford hasn’t announced the final hardware prices, and installation costs will vary. Plus, utility rules need to catch up if EV owners are going to take full advantage of bidirectional charging.
But this seems to be going in the right direction. If automakers can bring costs down and the industry can agree on consistent standards, having an EV that doubles as a home battery could eventually become a normal part of EV ownership rather than an expensive bonus feature.

FRP M3 Mini Bike Throws in Auto-Wheelie and 35 Miles of Range for a Little Over $2K
11 photos
Photo: FRP
It's not that difficult to buy a cheap and quite capable two-wheeler these days, thanks to the rapid growth of the electric mini bike segment. And the offers available keep growing in number, thanks to more and more players joining the party.
There's a good chance you haven't heard that much about a mini bike maker called FRP Moto. An offshoot of FRP Powersports, the California-based company has been playing the gas-based mini bike game for a while now, but this week, it unveiled its first-ever purpose-built electric two-wheeler.
The design is called M3, and it is powered by an electric drivetrain consisting of a permanent-magnet synchronous electric motor good for just four horsepower (5.5 peak, but it can only hold that for 17 seconds) and a removable 60V battery pack that gives it a maximum range of 35 miles (56 km). It takes up to nine hours to charge the thing using a 3A charger.
The bike's top speed is rated at 55 mph (89 kph), which is not a lot. Then again, that's not how the M3 plans to charm its customers: it will do that with the auto-wheelie feature it comes equipped with.
You see, the mini bike has three main riding gears, but it tops that off with two dedicated wheelie gears, a practice mode and an advanced mode. They can both be used at speeds of up to ten mph (16 mph), with braking power left in the control of the rider.
They both kick in as soon as the rider brings the front wheel up, and are used to hold the bike in that position thanks to a controller that constantly adjusts motor output to keep the bike balanced.
Going deeper into how the thing works, the throttle moves from controlling speed to setting the wheelie angle, which can be anywhere from 20 to 45 degrees. If the bike detects it tips past 58.5 degrees, it automatically comes out of wheelie mode.
The company says it decided to offer this feature to fulfil riders' needs to learn how to wheelie at their own pace
The FRP M3 also throws in a triple-clamp with suspension, 5.7-inch-wide SunF tires, and USB-A and USB-C ports. All of this is packed in a package that tips the scales at 121 pounds (55 kg) - light, but not flimsy, as it can support riders weighing almost double that, or as much as 210 pounds (95 kg).
FRP says it has already opened the order books for the mini bike, with deliveries expected to begin early next month. There are two versions on the table: the Basic that sells for $2,049.99, and the Plus that goes for $2,149.99 for the simple reason that it comes with a wheelie bar. There are five colors to choose from: gold, purple, black, red and white.

The Perfect Nordic-Style Tiny Home Is Budget-Friendly and Big Enough for Four
37 photos
Photo: Mobi House
A natural fall landscape is the perfect backdrop for this beautiful home on wheels that embodies all the best qualities of the Nordic aesthetic, but it’s actually flexible enough to fit in everywhere. The new Mobi River has it all, from a space-efficient layout to smart utilities and stunning views, and the best part is that it’s purposely meant to be affordable.
Mobi House grew from a small business founded by husband and wife Bartek and Kasia to the largest manufacturer of mobile homes in Poland and one of the most acclaimed manufacturers in Europe. It happened in less than a decade, and it started with the tiny house that Bartek built himself and lived in for two years, while living in Norway. Scandinavian style had a huge influence on the couple and, later, on the Mobi House creations, and it’s still present today.
As it continued to develop and expand, the Polish brand added new lines to its already impressive portfolio, developed in direct response to specific needs or trends on the market. One of them is the Invest Line. As the name suggests, it’s geared toward investors looking to get a quick, guaranteed return on their investment. The homes in this series are purposely budget-friendly, low-maintenance, and flexible, to address the needs of beginner entrepreneurs .
The Invest Line homes are built to weigh no more than 3.5 tons so that they can be registered as caravans. This allows owners to install them even in remote locations, and also relocate them easily when needed. Secondly, they are built with specific damage-resistant and scratch-resistant materials, and then equipped with appliances that are easy to replace; all of this translates to low maintenance and lower costs over time.
Photo: Mobi House Lastly, future owners have the option to add an integrated smart system that allows the remote control of basically all the main functions of the house, from access to lighting, heating, and air conditioning, all via a simple mobile application. All of these advantages transform the Invest Line homes into the perfect package for an entrepreneur looking to start a tiny house rental business or a small hospitality business.
Mobi River is a new and an old model at the same time. It has evolved from the popular Mobi Individual design, and it has now become a permanent part of the Invest Line range, under the name of Mobi River. In a nutshell, this could be described as the perfect Nordic-style tiny house for short-term living, both for families or investors. It’s highly compact, boasting less than 20 square meters (215 square feet) of floor space, yet it can accommodate up to four people.
The single-loft configuration includes a flexible lounge area that can serve as a ground-floor bedroom. The design itself takes the best of the Scandinavian aesthetic and gives it a modern-classic twist. You have core elements such as the oversized picture windows for excellent views, the natural tone and texture of wood, minimal furniture for a clean, clutter-free look, and a function-follows-form approach that makes the most of a small living space.
Modular furniture is one of the signature elements introduced by the Polish brands and present in almost all of its custom-builds. It takes space efficiency to the next level while complementing the minimalist approach to interior design. In the case of Mobi River, a couple of well-picked items change the functionality of the entire space, and it works like magic.
Photo: Mobi House First, you have a fold-down table and a couple of fold-down chairs in the small area between the actual lounge and the main entrance. When unfolded, this becomes an excellent dining setup or even a workspace. When folded, that entire area is freed for other activities or simply for a clutter-free look. It’s as simple as that.
As for the lounge itself, it can be furnished either with a custom-made raised bed that hides huge storage drawers underneath and that can double as a daybed during daytime, or with a standard convertible sofa. Either way, this open space is intended to function both as a lounge during the day and a bedroom at night, which is a common feature in almost all Nordic-style tiny homes.
The raised bed option adds considerable storage, which can be particularly important for families looking to invest in Mobi River as a vacation home or weekender. A tiny home that’s only 6.6-meters (21.6 feet) long and 2.5-meter (8 feet) wide doesn’t typically have a lot of room left for storage, which is one of the main reasons why Mobi River isn’t offered as a long-term accommodation option. Still, clever layout makes room for storage wherever possible.
This includes a custom-crafted closet near the main entrance, with side storage for outerwear and shoes, and conventional storage for clothes and personal items. The kitchen comes with its own custom-made cabinetry (laminated plywood and composite materials), enough for basic storage, and the bathroom is also equipped with a compact vanity.
Photo: Mobi House The kitchen doesn’t take up too much space inside this layout, which is another indication that this isn’t a tiny home built for permanent accommodation. Appliances include a compact under-counter fridge, a stove/oven, a built-in dishwasher, and a range hood. The same compact, space-saving approach turns this model’s loft into a minimalist, but practical bedroom.
It has the structure of an attic rather than a loft, with only a tiny window in the back instead of the typical horizontal windows on each side, and only enough floor space for a two-person bed mattress. Yes, this room counts as a two-person bedroom, but don’t expect the cozy comfort or the fancy features of a luxury tiny house loft. This goes for the access as well – there’s no staircase, which would have taken up way too much space.
The simple movable ladder that provided access to the loft bedroom is cleverly stored on the wall near the entrance area, so that it becomes almost invisible when not in use. Style-wise, the Nordic influence is reflected in the neutral color palette and minimalist décor (including the light fixtures). Natural light and the surrounding views become part of the décor, which is something that defines Scandinavian interiors.
The multi-purpose lounge/bedroom in particular looks and feels stunning thanks to not one, but two enormous panoramic windows that bring the outdoors in. It’s the classic Nordic recipe for a warm and cozy ambiance and an immersive living experience in the middle of nature. This is why Mobi River works best in a natural environment, where it can become a comfortable sanctuary for a deeper connection with nature and a truly relaxing experience.
Photo: Mobi House Mobi River is based on a timber frame, but its interior relies heavily on laminated plywood (an affordable alternative that is also low-maintenance and durable). The thermal insulation is meant to ensure year-round comfort, and customers have multiple choices for heating, including underfloor heating and air conditioning with a heating function. The house is delivered on a Lift &Go trailer by MH Trailers, which allows the chassis to be detached from the tiny house after installation.
A seamless blend of natural simplicity and smart, contemporary features, this tiny house takes the best of the Scandinavian aesthetic and elevates it for even better flexibility, while creating cozy comfort for up to four guests with minimal use of space.

BYD’s new flagship EV will be its largest and most luxurious electric sedan yet, potentially debuting two firsts for the company next week: Rolls-Royce-style coach doors and solid-state batteries.
BYD teases Yangwang Altior EV ahead of Nov 5 debut
BYD is better known for its low-cost electric cars, like the Seagull , a little hatchback that sells for under $10,000 in China.
The Chinese auto giant has greatly expanded its portfolio over the past few months and years. BYD now offers everything from entry-level EVs to three-row flagship SUVs, pickup trucks, electric supercars, and just about everything in between.
BYD has three sub-brands: Denza, FangChengBao, and Yangwang. It also has two main families under the BYD brand: the Dynasty and Ocean series.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Yangwang sits at the top of BYD’s brand hierarchy and showcases its latest breakthrough technologies.
Previously, Yangwang vehicles debuted on BYD’s quad-motor e4 platform, delivering a whopping 1,300 horsepower and featuring its DiSus-X intelligent body control system, which enables the vehicle to “dance,” jump, and drive on three wheels.
BYD Yangwang flagship sedan prototype (Source: Hu Xiaoqing)
For its next model, BYD is pushing further into the elite segment to take on ultra-luxury brands like Rolls-Royce, Bentley, and Mercedes-Maybach.
BYD revealed the name of its flagship ultra-luxury EV for the first time on Tuesday: the Yangwang Altior, along with a new teaser of the partially uncovered executive sedan.
Coming soon #YANGWANG #YANGWANGALTIOR pic.twitter.com/kFnu6X6csq — BYD Global (@BYDGlobal) October 27, 2026
Yangwang general manager Hu Xiaoqing said the name was chosen as an independent Chinese-English naming scheme. In China, it goes by DingYao. The “Ding” symbolizes stability and endurance, while “Yao” signifies radiant brilliance, or shining brightly like a star in the sky.
The English name Altior comes from Latin for “higher,” representing Yangwang’s relentless pursuit of ever-greater heights.
The new teaser comes after Hu revealed several images of the new Yangwang executive sedan testing for the first time last month.
BYD Yangwang flagship sedan prototype (Source: Hu Xiaoqing)
Although it was disguised, it appeared to be about the same shape and size as the Mercedes-Benz Maybach S-Class or Rolls-Royce Phantom. Local reports indicate it will be around 5,500 mm (216″) long.
HU confirmed for the first time last week that the global launch of the new flagship sedan will take place in the UAE, not in BYD’s home market of China.
BYD has not yet revealed a specific launch date, but the Yangwang sedan could make its first appearance as early as next week. According to CarNewsChina , citing “sources familiar with the project,” BYD is aiming to reveal the new flagship model in Dubai, UAE, around November 5.
Yangwang flagship electric sedan (Source: Zheng Yu)
Zheng Yu, Yangwang’s executive general manager, said the new model will feature “unprecedented disruptive technology,” but didn’t reveal specifics.
Although details are still limited, the ultra-luxury sedan was shown at BYD’s Flash Charging station, suggesting it will support megawatt flash charging.
It also features rear-hinged coach doors, a first for BYD. The flagship EV will reportedly be the first to feature BYD’s solid-state batteries.

Did you know you can still buy a low-mileage Lamborghini Gallardo ? Takes this Spyder, which is now listed for grabs in the United States of America, and it is an almost flawless example.
The seller, who reportedly bought it in August 2025, adding some 1,000 miles (1,600 km) since, stated that it came from a private collection before he wrote his name on the dotted line, adding that he has enjoyed bring it back to driving condition. However, since he is now ready to move on to this “next automotive toy,” he put it up for sale, and this is one machine that deserves a lot of attention, especially if you are into the Gallardo.
It’s a well-documented example that has only 5,300 miles (8,500 km) under its belt since new. The 2008 Lamborghini Gallardo Spyder in question has zero modifications, which makes it even more desirable, and other than some wear on the interior switchgear, there is nothing else wrong with. The Carfax report reveals that the modern-classic Italian supercar hasn’t been involved in any accidents, and there are also no mileage discrepancies for extra peace of mind.
The supercar has a Nero Perseus black exterior paint finish on top of a Bianco Polar interior that combines white and black leather upholstery and some white stitching. The two-tone leather upholstery, a power-operated soft top, power adjustable and heated seats, a dual-zone climate control system, a basic infotainment system, a nose-lift system, 19-inch Callisto wheels are mentioned in the ad that we will link toward the end of this story.
Photo: Cars&Bids This open-top Lamborghini Gallardo had its clutch wear test performed in September 2026, revealing a 43.11 percent wear, and that is also when an airbag module was replaced. The tires were rotated in July 2026, and in June, it had its engine oil and filter changed. The brake fluid, coolant, and front differential fluids were flushed, the batter was replaced, the engine oil and filter were changed, and the tires were replaced in September 2025, when the car had 4,334 miles (6,975 km) under its belt.
You do know what powers this model, don’t you? If you said a naturally aspirated V10, then you certainly know your Italian supercars. The 5.0-liter engine was officially good for 513 brake horsepower (520 ps/382 kW) and 376 pound-feet (510 Nm) of torque. It had the ability to sprint to 60 mph (97 kph) in a hair over 4-second mark, and if you kept the right pedal pinned to the floor, then it would run out of breath at 195 mph (314 kph). A six-speed automated manual transmission delivers everything to all four wheels.
In addition to the car , the next owner will get one key, and the usual lecture consisting of the owner’s manuals, as well as some service records, and even the window sticker. The latter reveals that this machine was over a quarter of a million dollars back in the day. The MSRP was $253,745, to be more precise, and something like this is now worth a lot less. In fact, you will have to prepare between $100,000 and $140,000 for one of these in today’s used car market.
The six-speed manual variant can cost upward of $200,000, and ultra-low mileage examples, which have less than 10,000 miles (16,000 km) under their belts, typically sell for between $135,000 and upward of $170,000. By Rainbow Nelson

Sudden tariff announcements, not tariff levels themselves, trigger costly cargo surges that terminals cannot absorb, delegates at TOC Americas in Cartagena were told.
Rather than destroying container trade, said TiL Group’s director for terminal investments in North America, Tom van Eynde, tariffs were relocating it, pointing to cargo shifting from Canadian ports into TiL’s US terminals as evidence.
“It has been somewhat of a wild ride over the past year, the past two years,” Mr van Eynde noted, referring to tariffs in the US being introduced and then cancelled. “They’re not really reducing the trade flows, they’re just relocating them.”
While the terminal operator saw a reduction in certain trade flows to the US through Canadian ports, he said these were then automatically being picked up by TiL terminals in US ports. Expecting the situation to be “a temporary thing”, Mr van Eynde said he expected disruption to settle once tariffs hit a range of 10% to 15% – “at that kind of level we see very little impact anymore on the volume.”
The real damage, he said, came less from the tariffs themselves than from sudden announcements that triggered a rush of cargo before a deadline, only for conditions to return to normal once it passed.
“That is probably the element that has hurt us most,” he said.
Carriers can respond to a surge by chartering extra vessels and running a new swing, which Mr van Eynde said had even lifted freight rates in their favour. Terminal capacity could not move at the same speed, building more takes years to plan and permit, he said, and by the time it was ready, demand may already have shifted again.
“We are the ones taking the biggest hit from these kind of things,” he continued.
Despite the uncertainty, Mr van Eynde said TiL was investing more aggressively than ever, pointing to its position as the main terminal partner for MSC, the biggest carrier and still growing faster than the market, he added, as a way to offset the political risk in its portfolio.
Deploying extra gangs and equipment could absorb a sudden peak, he explained, but it brought congestion to the yard and the rail operation, and a higher cost per box.
“It’s certainly eating out of our margins,” he said.

source_document.body:
The data center buildout underway across North America is charging ahead at full speed and may even surpass original forecasts. Facility owners are no longer planning incremental expansions. The demand for data, driven by the rapid adoption and maturation of artificial intelligence (AI), now has them planning in gigawatts. Demand has increased; expectations have changed, yet many infrastructure and trade-off assumptions still linger, holding data centers back from reaching their full potential.
One of those assumptions is that reliability and sustainability are competing priorities. There is a longstanding belief that data center owners must choose between running hard and running clean. At the power infrastructure layer, that simply isn’t the case anymore. Electrical decisions made during design can help data center owners accomplish both without compromise.
The Scale of the Demand Problem
Understanding the infrastructure challenge requires clarity on what is actually driving demand. While AI workloads are the fastest-growing source of data center power demand, they currently represent only approximately 14% of total consumption, according to recent Goldman Sachs research , with cloud computing and traditional storage workloads accounting for the remainder. AI’s share is rising rapidly, but the sheer volume of baseline data storage growth means the buildout challenge extends well beyond AI infrastructure alone.
According to a 2025 Synergy Research Group report , nearly 1,300 hyperscale data centers exist globally, with roughly 770 more planned. Meanwhile, AI-driven data center power needs are projected to rise 175% during the same period.
Electricity now flows through an interconnected ecosystem of generation, data centers, AI platforms, and end users, making infrastructure decisions foundational to both performance and sustainability. Source: Southwire
In regions where grid connections cannot keep pace with development timelines, island power and microgrid solutions have become standard stop-gap measures. These bridge strategies sustain operations until utility capacity catches up, but they are not long-term infrastructure solutions. The data centers built today will need reliable, sustainable solutions that help them power smarter and operate greener to keep them running smoothly over their expected 20-year service life.
The geographic footprint of this buildout is also shifting. Traditional hyperscale clusters in Northern Virginia, Phoenix, and Dallas have either saturated available power or faced significant community resistance. Development is moving to markets where land and power are more accessible, including rural corridors in the Southeast, the Rocky Mountain region, and the Plains states, where weather exposure, environmental conditions, and grid infrastructure pose challenges distinct from those in established markets. High heat, ice storms, and high-wind events must be considered in the design phase to specify appropriate solutions.
Powering Smarter: From Transmission to Distribution
Overhead power cables are the first critical link in a data center’s power delivery chain. By specifying high-temperature, low-sag overhead conductors designed for extreme climate conditions, data center owners can increase ampacity and improve transmission reliability and performance, while also utilizing existing rights-of-way and towers to reduce environmental disruption and the carbon footprint of new corridor construction.
Proper specification is equally important for power crossing the facility threshold. Both medium-voltage (MV) and high-voltage (HV) systems require advanced insulation and jacket materials capable of withstanding heat, moisture, and mechanical stress across the full range of conditions the facility may encounter. Whether inside or outside the building, undersized conductors, those inadequately rated for actual load profiles, or those not suited to the environment can degrade and cause line losses, increasing the risk of unplanned outages and shortening service life.
High-temperature, low-sag conductors and properly specific MV/HV systems increase ampacity, reduce line loss, and extend infrastructure life across the full power delivery chain. Source: Southwire
Proper specification across the full power delivery chain, from overhead transmission through MV and HV distribution, is where reliability and sustainability intersect most directly. A conductor engineered for its actual operating environment lasts longer, degrades more slowly and predictably, and requires less frequent replacement. That translates directly to fewer rip-and-replace cycles, less material waste, and lower embodied carbon over the facility’s service life. The infrastructure decisions that protect uptime are, by definition, the same decisions that reduce long-term environmental impact.
Operating Greener: Sustainability Begins with Specification
Leading hyperscalers have moved sustainability requirements upstream into their procurement processes. Several converging pressures are driving this shift. Corporate net-zero commitments have moved from aspirational to contractual, with major operators now required to account for Scope 3 emissions. At the same time, community opposition to data center development has intensified in established markets. Planning boards and advocacy groups are scrutinizing construction materials and practices, as well as operational energy use and carbon emissions.
Operators who cannot demonstrate verified environmental commitments at the materials level are finding it harder to secure community approvals. The result is that sustainability criteria, once addressed late in procurement, are now entering the specification conversation at the same stage as performance requirements. Recycled copper offers a significant sustainability advantage, requiring about 85% less energy to produce than primary copper from ore. For data center owners with Scope 3 reporting obligations, the embodied carbon in wire and cable is often overlooked in favor of the more obvious sources in concrete and steel. Manufacturers producing electrical components with recycled copper provide a verifiable path to reduce that footprint without compromising conductor performance, giving procurement teams documented reductions they can report with confidence.
For facilities approaching the 10- to 15-year mark in their service life, responsible infrastructure modernization is key. Innovative retrofit approaches for aging cable systems can extend asset life and avoid the full carbon cost associated with sourcing new materials, manufacturing, transportation, installation, and waste. Modernizing existing infrastructure where technically appropriate is a sustainability practice that remains underutilized relative to its potential.
For greenfield or brownfield projects, Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs) are the gold standard for providing third-party-verified, cradle-to-gate carbon data in accordance with ISO 14025. Operators can incorporate that data directly into bids and sustainability reports. For hyperscalers, EPD availability is increasingly a specification requirement—a condition of doing business rather than a consideration that is addressed late in the evaluation.
Material transparency through EPDs and the use of recycled metals provide data center operators with documented Scope 3 emissions reductions tied directly to infrastructure specification. Source: Southwire
Specification decisions made at the design stage have both performance and sustainability implications that extend 15 to 20 years into the future. A facility built with electrical components engineered for actual operating conditions and with verified material transparency through EPDs is better positioned to meet both performance imperatives and decarbonization commitments.
The Coordination Imperative
Early coordination among data center owners, utilities, engineers, contractors, and manufacturers will ensure performance and sustainability are designed in from the beginning. In an environment defined by compressed timelines, constrained supply chains, and communities that are increasingly skeptical of data center development, coordination becomes a competitive advantage. Treating electrical infrastructure decisions as a systems problem rather than a procurement checklist is what keeps projects on schedule and sustainability commitments intact.
From a performance standpoint, the case for early coordination is straightforward. When MV cable lead times can exceed 50 weeks, treating conductors as a downstream procurement item rather than integrating them into the coordination schedule alongside switchgear, transformers, and uninterruptible power systems has immediate and cascading consequences.
When gear arrives on site, but conductors are unavailable, improperly staged, or misaligned with routing constraints, the schedule impact ripples across mechanical, structural, and commissioning scopes simultaneously. Capacity agreements, in which manufacturers hold production slots against an owner’s multi-year forecast, offer operators peace of mind that construction timelines won’t get pushed out despite constrained supply chains.
Utilities are equally critical partners in coordination. Sharing multi-year capacity forecasts with utility providers enables them to anticipate requirements and begin building or modernizing transmission lines to handle the data center load. By working with utilities early, data center owners are more likely to have the transmission infrastructure they need available on time, keeping construction and time-to-power timelines on track.
Early collaboration also delivers sustainability benefits, alongside performance improvements. When routing geometry is optimized during design, unnecessary splice points are eliminated, reducing material waste and the associated carbon footprint. Pull studies conducted during design inform routing decisions and eliminate unnecessary complexity before it reaches the field. Defining delivery sequencing and storage requirements in advance prevents product damage and the rework it causes.
Designing for the Full Service Life
The data centers being planned and built today will operate for two decades or more. Power infrastructure decisions made today will determine whether a facility can handle the load profiles of 2035 and beyond, withstand increasingly severe weather events, and satisfy tightening sustainability reporting requirements.
Powering smarter and operating greener are not competing objectives to be balanced against each other in the design process. At the infrastructure layer, they are expressions of the same discipline: specifying infrastructure for actual conditions, full-service life, and verified performance rather than minimum acceptable thresholds. The industry has long accepted the reliability-versus-sustainability trade-off as an engineering reality, but it is not a technical constraint; it is a planning failure.
Data centers built on thoughtful specifications, verified material transparency, and early coordination need not choose between running hard and running clean. At the infrastructure layer, they don’t compete; they complement one another.
— Jack Graves is VP, Strategic Verticals, at Southwire . Read more about energizing the digital era here.

By Gavin van Marle
27 October 2026
Hong Kong-headquartered intra-Asia carrier SITC has seen its share price hit record highs in recent days after its board last week voted to approve a special dividend, returning some HK$2.7bn (US$344m) to shareholders.
“The board is pleased to announce that it has resolved the declaration and payment of the special dividend of HK$1 (equivalent to US$0.13) per ordinary share of the company to be payable to the shareholders whose names appear on the company’s register of members at the close of business on 11 December 2026,” it said in a Hong Kong Stock Exchange (HKSE) filing on Friday.
According to the CapitalIQ platform, 49.1% of SITC’s stock is freely floated on the HKSE, with the remaining 51.9% held by a British Virgin Islands company, and together amount to 2.71bn shares out.
Its share price closed on Monday at HK$47.9, just shy of the record HK$52 seen on 13 October, shortly after the special dividend was first proposed.
SITC 10-year share price (Source: HKSE)
It is further sign that investors in shipping stocks are having bumper year, in what Loadstar Premium’s DeskOne has labelled the “Shipping $ Series”, a moniker prompted by a similar “extraordinary special dividend” issued earlier this month by non-operating shipowner Danaos.
The Greek shipowner, listed on the New York Stock Exchange, has also seen its stock price break all records in recent weeks, and notified the market it was issuing a $5 special dividend to shareholders in mid-October.
Danaos five-year share price (Source: NYSE)
Meanwhile, approval of SITC’s special dividend followed the release of its unaudited operational performance for the first nine months of the year, which showed the intra-Asia carrier remarkably insulated from most of the geopolitical events battering large parts of the shipping industry.
It reported carrying 2.91m teu during the period, a 5.9% increase on the 2.75m teu it carried in the first nine months of 2025.
Meanwhile, according to Container Trades Statistics (CTS) data from the first eight months of 2026, intra-Asia volume growth stood at 8.6%.
Source: CTS
Although this could be interpreted as SITC losing market share, given the continued strength of the intra-Asia trades it is unclear whether SITC could have taken advantage of that market growth, considering the rather limited capacity of its vessels.
As Alphaliner explained in a September analysis, while SITC is the sixth-largest intra-Asia carrier in terms of fleet capacity, the five larger carriers are all mainline operators that deploy considerably larger ships in the trade than the specialised regional carriers. Alphaliner data shows the average size of a deepsea carrier’s intra-Asia vessel at 2,699 teu, “more than double the 1,338 teu average for regional carriers”.
SITC’s average ship size is 1,444 teu.
Alphaliner added: “SITC, the leading regional carrier in intra-Asia, makes the point vividly: it runs 109 ships, but its considerably smaller average vessel size leaves its total capacity at 157,000 teu, well behind Maersk and Cosco, putting SITC in sixth spot.
“This is in line with SITC’s focus on direct services to smaller and niche ports in Asia, rather than competing on scale. SITC is the only carrier on the list besides Maersk (108 ships) and Cosco (122 ships) that operates a fleet of more than 100 vessels in the region,” Alphaliner wrote.

In a Phase 1 study, treatment with Incyte’s KRAS G12D inhibitor in combination with standard-of-care chemotherapy elicited an 89% confirmed objective response rate in patients with a type of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, leading analysts to draw comparisons with Revolution Medicines’ zoldonrasib.
Incyte’s KRAS G12D inhibitor achieved an 89% confirmed objective response rate in an early-stage clinical trial for a type of pancreatic cancer, notching another step forward for a patient community that, until earlier this year, had few options.
The updated results are from an ongoing Phase 1 study of Incyte’s INCB161734, also known as zecdarasib, plus chemo in 54 patients with metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) with a KRAS G12D mutation. If the result holds through further clinical development, the biotech could someday find itself on the market against pancreatic cancer rival Revolution Medicines.
The new data make Incyte a “firm contender” in the G12D race, analysts at BMO Capital Markets said in a note to investors on Monday.
INCB161734 elicited 89% and 81% objective response rates—a secondary outcome measure in the trial—for confirmed and pending results, respectively, when combined with the chemotherapy regimen mFOLFIRINOX. This pairing also showed 100% disease control rate, another secondary endpoint, and six-month progression-free survival (PFS) rate of 90%, the company said Monday during an oral session at the European Society of Medical Oncology in Madrid.
Combined with a different chemotherapy regimen called GEMNabP, the drug’s objective response rate was lower, at 69% confirmed and 58% pending, with a disease control rate of 96% and six-month PFS of 80%.
As for safety—the Phase 1 trial’s primary endpoint—the candidate’s profile was “manageable” in both PDAC and colorectal cancers, another focus of the study, Pablo Cagnoni, president and global head of Research and Development at Incyte, said in a statement on Monday.
In both groups, totaling 103 patients, adverse events included diarrhea, nausea and decreased neutrophil count. The mFOLFIRINOX arms included incidence of vomiting, but no patients discontinued treatment. With GEMNabP, the adverse events included anemia, and one patient discontinued the regimen. The safety profile “appears broadly consistent” with the established profiles of the standard-of-care chemo regimens, BMO wrote.
While RevMed’s recently approved RAS inhibitor Rasonque also addresses PDAC with G12D mutations, there is plenty of room for new treatment options. These individuals saw a lower objective response rate than those with other mutations, such as G12V, according to FDA review documents published by the FDA earlier this month.

And the G12D PDAC competitive landscape remains neck and neck, analysts from RBC Capital Markets said in an Oct. 26 note.
BMO compared Incyte’s candidate to RevMed’s zoldonrasib, which posted objective response rates of 82% in combination with mFOLFIRINOX and 61% with GEMNabP chemotherapies, according to the analysts. Against zoldonrasib’s benchmark, Incyte’s INCB161734 “appears at least competitive on response, particularly with mFOLFIRINOX,” they wrote.
Compared with zoldonrasib, Incyte’s drug has a longer duration of exposure, providing both more time for treatment but also for adverse events to kick in, Cagnoni said during an investor presentation at ESMO. Analysts pointed to these factors as a small but potentially important differentiator between the two drug candidates.
The sales opportunity for INCB161734 could reach $1.4 billion in PDAC, BMO said, while Truist analysts said Incyte’s drug could get an earlier start in the market if the ongoing global Phase 3 Dawn-303 study, which combines INCB161734 to investigators’ choice of chemo regimens in first-line PDAC, generates a solid objective response rate analysis around the middle of next year. Incyte also plans to embark on a Phase 3 trial in the adjuvant setting next year.
The nuances of addressing KRAS mutations will likely play a role, RBC analysts said. “We think ‘734’s opportunity will likely come down to where G12Ds ultimately fit into the PDAC paradigm,” including whether more differentiation emerges as overall survival and other long-term data mature, and whether chemo-free combos become the standard.

Police recovered approximately $54,000 in stolen Hot Wheels merchandise following a freight train burglary in Colton, California. A witness called 911 around 3 a.m. Thursday, October 22, reporting suspicious activity near railroad tracks. Officers spotted a black Chevrolet Silverado leaving the area and initiated a traffic stop. The investigation ended with one arrest and 350 boxes of toy cars in police custody.
According to video released by the Colton Police Department , the caller reported people stealing merchandise near Maple Street. An officer positioned himself near Seventh Street and La Cadena Drive while monitoring the surrounding roads. Footage shows authorities following the pickup before stopping its driver. The man exited with his hands on his head, and officers took him into custody.
The department confirmed the recovery in its October 22 Facebook announcement. Authorities booked the suspect into West Valley Detention Center on suspicion of burglary, grand theft and possession of stolen property. The department did not identify the individual in its public announcement.
In a response to FreightWaves, Colton Police Department representative Jillian Nunez provided additional details about the investigation. Officers discovered an open Maersk shipping container and additional merchandise along nearby railroad tracks. Investigators identified Mattel as the cargo owner, while BNSF Railway took possession of the recovered property. Nunez confirmed that authorities will return the merchandise to its owner through the appropriate process.
Colton police documented boxes of recovered Hot Wheels merchandise following the October 22 burglary. (Photo: Colton Police Department)
Another rail cargo theft in Southern California
The Colton, California, arrest follows several freight theft investigations involving BNSF Railway shipments across Southern California. In August, deputies recovered $150,000 in New Balance shoes following a boxcar burglary near Daggett, California. In September, a container caught fire during a burglary aboard a moving BNSF train near Riverside, California . In October, Los Angeles detectives uncovered $1 million in stolen BNSF and Union Pacific merchandise at a Whittier, California, retailer.
The Colton Police Department maintains an active enforcement contract with BNSF Railway to address cargo theft and related criminal activity. Nunez confirmed the agreement in her response to FreightWaves. Officials did not disclose the contract’s duration or specific enforcement responsibilities.
A closer look at cartons of Hot Wheels merchandise recovered during the October 22 investigation in Colton, California. (Photo: Colton Police Department)
Investigation leaves questions about container access
Colton police believe additional individuals may have participated in the theft. Nunez confirmed that detectives reached that assessment through witness statements and information gathered during the investigation. Authorities continue examining the circumstances surrounding the burglary under case number 26-07172. The department declined to speculate about possible connections to other Inland Empire cargo thefts.
Investigators have not confirmed whether thieves accessed the container while the train was moving or stationary. Police also have not explained how suspects opened the equipment or whether they recovered every missing item. Authorities have not disclosed the shipment’s intended destination. FreightWaves contacted BNSF Railway for additional comment, but the railroad had not responded before publication.
Why it matters
A witness’s 911 call helped officers intercept a vehicle carrying $54,000 in stolen merchandise. The incident highlights the importance of timely reporting and coordinated responses to suspected rail cargo theft.

Giugiaro's Peralta D Is the Hand-Made Copper-Body Gran Tourer, No One's Rich Enough To Have Another
22 photos
Photo: GFG Style
You’d never thought that, in this speed-crazed, high-tech-junkie society of ours, automotive design would take a step toward the very beginnings of man. And yet, the bold Italians behind the Peralta D one-off have done just that – catapulted the personal transportation paradigm straight to the copper age, when homo Sapiens were just learning to fabricate tools out of pure copper. This is what GFG Style proposes some ten millennia later – a car made out of copper.
Throughout the history of automotive engineering, carmakers have relied on a familiar roster of materials to shape their vehicles’ bodies. Steel has long served as the traditional industrial workhorse, while lightweight aluminum, crafted wood, molded fiberglass, exotic carbon fiber, and various specialized alloys have all taken turns defining the silhouettes of modern transportation.
Yet, one question has rarely crossed the minds of automotive designers: when did a manufacturer ever think of sculpting an entire car shell out of pure copper?
Well, that moment has arrived right now, because GFG Style just made it happen. While copper is typically reserved for electrical wiring, plumbing, or heavy industrial applications, its employment in outer automotive shells has been virtually non-existent. Although this noble, malleable metal has been known to mankind since the dawn of civilization, it took a daring bespoke project to finally hammer it into a functional, rolling sculpture for the road.
(Take “hammering” literally, please, as we can see in the embedded video at the bottom of this story. Soft metals have traditionally been shaped with wooden mallets, which are gentle enough with the material to not destroy it upon impact, but strong enough to ply it according to the craftsman’s plans).
Photo: GFG Style Outside of heavy industry, copper has always found its most celebrated traditional uses in heirloom kitchenware and moonshine stills. For centuries, giant simmering cauldrons, heavy preserving pans, and intricate distillation alembics have been shaped by master artisans relying on just two basic assets: a simple set of hand tools and an immense reservoir of metal-working skills.
Taking that exact same ancestral craft of beating raw sheets over anvils and applying it to a modern supercar chassis is a bold leap across centuries of metallurgy. One that pays homage not just to manufacturing greatness, but to the very essence of our species’ evolution astray from the rest of the animal kingdom.
The organization behind this achievement is GFG Style, an advanced styling consultancy established in 2015 in Moncalieri, near Turin, Italy, by the legendary father-and-son duo Giorgetto and Fabrizio Giugiaro. Giorgetto is celebrated the world over as one of the most prolific automotive designers in history, while Fabrizio brings over 30 years of expertise in car design and architecture.
Photo: GFG Style Together, the pair have developed over 200 prototypes and more than 300 production models for numerous global manufacturers. Not a single one of their creations has gone unnoticed, or has ever been lost in the vast sea of automotive happenings (or mishaps, but the Giugiaros have never been known for making “alright” designs).
Their latest creation stems from a close friendship and creative collaboration with Mexican entrepreneur and car collector Carlos Peralta. Following the enthusiastic reception of their previous joint project, the one-off Peralta S, the collector commissioned a second bespoke vehicle.
Officially unveiled on October 24 at the prestigious 2026 Pastejé Automotive Invitational in Mexico, the new supercar is christened the Peralta D. While the previous model honored the commissioner's sons, the letter “D” celebrates his daughters and the Italian word "donne," meaning women.
Photo: GFG Style Personally overseen at every stage by Fabrizio Giugiaro, the Peralta D is a striking 2+2 Gran Turismo coupe defined by a monolithic form and minimalist geometric harmony. When viewed from above, the sleek, uninterrupted surfaces appear continuous, as if drawn with a single pencil stroke.
A pronounced waistline divides the exterior into two distinct zones: a lower body hammered entirely by hand from pure copper, and an upper canopy crafted from mirrored glass treated to replicate the warm hue of the metal.
Beneath this artisanal copper skin lies a modern structural architecture. The hand-beaten body panels are supported by a rigid carbon-fiber structure mounted onto a lightweight aluminum chassis (I told you so). To maintain pure visual elegance, all exterior carbon-fiber elements, including the integrated front blade spoiler and rear tailpipes, are deliberately concealed from plain sight.
The coupe rides on anthracite black wheels featuring a retro-futuristic geometric pattern inspired by the 1970s that enhances the visual impact of the bodywork.
Photo: GFG Style The vehicle derives its mechanical platform and energy source from the modern Maserati GranTurismo. While the Turin design house has kept exact exterior dimensions, curb weight, and specific engine output figures closely guarded for this private commission, utilizing top-of-the-line Maserati mechanical components is bound to deliver genuine supercar performance and grand touring dynamics.
Even the fuel cap is integrated into the geometric harmony of the copper panels, confirming an internal combustion engine beneath the sculpted metal. Which makes perfect sense, since fire and copper have been humanity’s long-standing pillars of evolution ever since we decided to make tools.
Both the front and rear fascias are punctuated by sharp blades of light and geometric diamond-shaped grilles crafted from solid-machined, laser-cut aluminum. These grilles integrate and conceal the functional lamps to create a dramatic "shadow lights" effect. Noticeably absent from the flanks are traditional side doors.
Photo: GFG Style Instead, cabin ingress is achieved through a sophisticated forward-lifting dome that maintains independent side windows, evolving the single-motion canopy concept introduced on the earlier Peralta S. believe it or not, Giugiaro is copying shamelessly on this one. He’s copying himself, though – his 1963 self who crafted the one-off Chevrolet Corvair Testudo, a fabulous machine with the exact same forward-tilting gadgetry.
To solve the age-old problem of cramped rear-seat entry in two-door coupes, Fabrizio Giugiaro paired the front canopy with an innovative rear gull-wing opening mechanism that requires no underlying structural pillars. This clever engineering solution provides effortless access to the back seats and pays direct homage to the historic gull-wing rear lids his father Giorgetto developed for the classic De Tomaso Mangusta back in 1967.
Inside the four-seat cabin, the monolithic exterior theme continues through ergonomic seats upholstered in metallic-effect leather that echoes the warm copper tones outside. The hides on the seats, dashboard, and door panels are complemented by perforated Alcantara inserts and stitched together using genuine copper thread.
Photo: GFG Style The symmetrical dashboard features a digital instrument cluster on the left for the driver, balanced on the right by a dedicated passenger makeup station complete with cosmetic compartments and a monitor that doubles as an illuminated mirror.
Tucked neatly into the rear section of the center console is a final bespoke luxury touch: a retractable refrigerator engineered to hold a bottle of champagne alongside four custom drinking glasses crafted, naturally, from pure copper. I told you mankind has been very fond of copper for several reasons – and one of those revolves around turning fruits and vegetables into liquid joy. The Italians have just created one more reason for us to worship element 29 in chemistry’s periodic table.

NEW DELHI — India’s defense exports to Europe have surged, driven largely by demand for ammunition and artillery shells as European countries ramp up military spending amid Russia’s war in Ukraine.
The rising exports could pave the way for deeper industrial cooperation between the two sides.
Indian Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh said that demand linked to the European Union’s “ReArm Europe” initiative, combined with India’s expanding defense manufacturing base, is boosting exports. He spoke Oct 23. at an event in New Delhi.
Singh cited a Bloomberg report that found a sharp increase in India’s exports of ammunition and related products to Europe.
India exported at least $872 million worth of ammunition in the four years since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, a more than 1,600% increase compared with the preceding four-year period, according to the report , which cited data from Trade Data Monitor.
Central and East European countries including Romania, Slovenia, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Bulgaria, Croatia, and Poland were among the biggest customers.
Ammunition exports have risen sharply since 2024 as European countries replenish stocks and strengthen defense capabilities following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, analysts say. The exports include artillery shells, small-caliber ammunition, mortars, propellants and explosives.
European destinations accounted for 40% of Indian global exports of arms and ammunition in the last financial year, according to Samuel Rajiv, Research Fellow at the Manohar Parrikar Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses in New Delhi.
He said this surge could translate into a long-term trend. “There will be greater opportunities for India due to Europe’s greater focus on defense, which will result in a lot of money going into the transformation of its defense industrial base,” said Rajiv. “At the same time, Indian exports will gain momentum not just because of Europe’s requirements but the steps India is taking to expand its own defense manufacturing base.”
Indian exports could also get a fillip as tariffs on arms and ammunition from India become lower when a free trade agreement concluded between India and the European Union takes effect in the coming year.
New Delhi is also seeking a broader role in Europe’s defense market through industrial partnerships. Defense Secretary Singh said India wants to establish joint ventures with European companies in India, while Indian companies would seek partnerships in Europe to gain access to government defense procurement programs.
Russia is not an option for Europe, that is over. Dinakar Peri, Carnegie India
Analysts say although it remains to be seen whether India and the EU can build more sustained defense industrial ties, partnering with each other is emerging as a viable option for both sides as Europe seeks to diversify its supply chains.
“India offers that scale, size and ecosystem as well as trust as Europe tries to build resilience from the United States. Russia is not an option for Europe, that is over. China has its own red flags in many ways in strategic areas and critical domains. So that leaves very few options available,” says Dinakar Peri, Fellow in the Security Studies Program at Carnegie India.
At the same time, India has also been working to diversify its defense relationships given its longstanding dependence on foreign suppliers, including the United States. “So a closer partnership with Europe also works for India,” he said.
Pointing out that several American, French, and Israeli contractors have already integrated Indian vendors into their supply chains, analysts say the EU can make India its sourcing hub for a range of items.
However New Delhi’s longstanding military ties with Russia could raise concerns in some European capitals as India eyes deeper defense partnerships with the EU.
“It remains to be seen whether this will become an obstacle to deeper defense industrial ties with the EU,” according to Peri. “Bilaterally, India already has strong defense relationships with countries such as France, but it is unclear how the EU as a bloc will view India’s military ties with Moscow.”

Lectric eBikes, the largest electric bike company in the US by just about any metric you can measure, has just unveiled its latest model: the Lectric XP Lite3 . And with a starting price of just $799 , the new lightweight folding electric bike is continuing the company’s tradition of packing surprisingly impressive features into remarkably affordable e-bikes.
The XP Lite2 had been widely considered the best bang-for-your-buck option in the ultra-budget category, offering an affordable yet punchy Class 2 e-bike for a song, despite still coming from a reputable US-based company with strong reputation for warranty and support.
Now, the third-generation model builds on what has become one of the most successful budget e-bike platforms in the country, bringing a long list of upgrades designed to make the bike easier to ride, fold, transport, and live with.
And perhaps most importantly, Lectric has managed to keep that familiar $799 starting price that debuted on the original XP Lite1 all the way back in 2022 .
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The Lectric XP Lite3 gets a major upgrade
The new Lectric XP Lite3 weighs just 49 lb (22.2 kg), making it one of the lighter options in Lectric’s extensive lineup of folding electric bikes. That’s still no featherweight, partly due to Lectric’s insistence on not neutering the bike’s performance, but it’s still a solid 10-20 lb lighter than the average direct-to-consumer e-bike these days.
The bike retains the compact folding design that made its predecessors popular with everyone from college students to RV owners, but introduces a redesigned frame with improved ergonomics and a reinforced folding latch borrowed from the company’s flagship XP4 model .
New quick-release pedals further reduce the bike’s storage footprint, making it easier to squeeze into a car trunk, apartment closet, or RV storage compartment.
Despite its compact dimensions, the XP Lite3 can support a maximum payload of 275 lb (125 kg) and accommodates riders ranging from 4’8” to 6’2”.
The bike reaches speeds of up to 20 mph (32 km/h) and offers up to 40 miles (64 km) or 80 miles (128 km) of range in Eco mode, though expect significantly less range when using higher-power pedal assist or throttle-only riding. The range discrepancy comes from two different battery offerings. The base model features a 374 Wh battery, while the long-range version has nearly twice the capacity at 672 Wh.
Power comes from Lectric’s Stealth M24 motor, which is rated at 300W continuous but over 800 peak watts. The motor combines with Lectric’s pedal assist selector to offer five levels of pedal assist that are personalizable, letting riders dial in exactly how much boost they’d like on their ride. Riders also get a twist throttle, a more comfortable style of throttle enabled by the lack of shifters crowding the bars on this single-speed e-bike.
Several other upgrades help the XP Lite3 punch above its weight class, including integrated rear turn signals, a bright 3.5-inch full-color display brought over from other recently launched models in the Lectric lineup, and a redesigned LevelUp Lite rear rack with new mounting possibilities.
Stopping power comes from Star Union 602 hydraulic disc brakes with thicker 2.3 mm rotors, another welcome feature on a bike at this price point.
Lectric is also offering a Gates Carbon Belt Drive version of the XP Lite3, giving riders a cleaner, quieter, and virtually maintenance-free alternative to a traditional chain drivetrain. That Gates belt drive model fetches a $100 premium, but is likely worth it for those who value the cleaner, maintenance-free alternative that is likely to outlast the bike itself.
The chain-drive version comes in Arctic White, Blue Mist, Matte Grey, and Matte Lavender, while the belt-drive model is offered in JW Black and Ballerina Pink.
Lectric continues to redefine affordable e-bikes
It’s difficult to overstate just how much Lectric has changed the American electric bicycle industry.
The Phoenix, Arizona-based company has grown into the country’s largest e-bike brand by both sales volume and the total number of e-bikes on the road. In doing so, it has become one of the most recognizable names in affordable electric transportation.
But Lectric didn’t get there by simply building cheap electric bikes.
Instead, the company helped revolutionize what consumers should expect from a budget-friendly e-bike, combining capable hardware, practical designs, and aggressive pricing with something that has historically been missing from much of the low-cost e-bike market: a real American company standing behind the product.
While countless inexpensive e-bikes sold online come from little-known overseas brands with questionable long-term support, Lectric has built its reputation around US-based customer service, accessible replacement parts, and a company that riders can actually reach when something goes wrong.
That’s a big part of what has made the XP Lite series so important.
Since its introduction, the XP Lite series has arguably set the standard for what an entry-level electric bike should be. It isn’t necessarily the most powerful, fastest, or fanciest e-bike on the road, but it delivers the essentials at a price that opens electric cycling to an entirely new audience.
And importantly, it does so without requiring riders to gamble on an unknown brand.
The XP Lite3 continues that formula, adding features like hydraulic disc brakes, integrated turn signals, and a color display that would have been difficult to imagine on a $799 e-bike just a few years ago.
Electrek’s Take
I’ve been following Lectric since the company’s earliest days, and it’s been fascinating to watch how the brand has consistently raised the bar for affordable electric bikes. I rode one of Lectric’s first 10 bikes off their nascent production line all the way back in 2019, and I think they’d agree that few people outside the company know the brand better than I do. So I can say that, without a doubt, this is one of the company’s most important launches to date because of how it revolutionizes how much bike someone can get without stretching their budget farther than they have to. And at a time when inflation is still rising unchecked and fuel prices are through the roof, this is what the industry needs more than ever.
Keep in mind that the $799 price tag for the XP Lite3 announced today is the same price that the original XP Lite carried back in 2022, despite that value ballooning to $939 in 2026 dollars due to rising inflation.
$799 in 2022 would be equivalent to $939.19 today, meaning Lectric has effectively been decreasing its prices over the last few years to maintain affordability for consumers (Source: US Bureau of Labor Statistics )
What impresses me most isn’t necessarily any single feature on the new XP Lite3. It’s the combination of all those features at a price that remains accessible to so many riders.
Hydraulic brakes, a color display, integrated turn signals, a refined folding mechanism, and even the option for a Gates belt drive? That’s quite a lot of bike for the money. And remember, the performance is still there. This is still a 48V e-bike with a legit 20 mph (32 km/h) top speed on throttle and pedal assist.
Sure, there are lighter e-bikes out there, and there are certainly more premium models with fancier components. But that’s not really the point of the XP Lite.
The point is to make electric biking accessible without making it feel like a compromise at every turn.
And when you consider that you’re getting all of this from the biggest e-bike company in the country, complete with US-based support and a proven track record, it’s hard to argue with the value proposition.
The original XP Lite helped establish what a good affordable electric bike could be. The XP Lite3 looks ready to move that benchmark forward once again.
And on a personal note, not only do I want my own Lectric XP Lite3 now, but I think my wife’s new e-bike will soon be an XP Lite3 in Ballerina Pink with a Gates belt drive. Remember, “Happy wife, happy life!”

The corporate investor arms of Eli Lilly, Sanofi and Pfizer have participated in billions worth of venture capital rounds, but GV is the industry’s biggest spender.
The biggest corporate spender in biotech isn’t the investment arm of a well-known Big Pharma. Rather, Google parent Alphabet’s GV earns that title, having participated in deals worth a cumulative $5.23 billion since the beginning of 2025.
This total—which was spread across 20 deals, according to data collected by PitchBook—makes the tech firm one of biotech’s most influential venture capital investors.
GV lists hundreds of biotechs on its portfolio, among them some of the biggest newsmakers in biotech, such as pancreatic cancer biotech Revolution Medicines. GV invested in RevMed’s $100 million series C in 2019, exiting when the company went public in February 2020.
GV tends to participate in larger deals, according to a PitchBook analysis. The firm was founded in 2009 and currently has $13 billion in assets under management.
Lilly USA is the most prolific dealmaker in life sciences VC, participating in 38 total deals since January 1, but the total worth of these transactions was lower than GV’s spend, at a cumulative $2.5 billion. If you add in the pharma’s Asia unit—Lilly Asia Fund, which is separate—Eli Lilly had its fingerprints on 63 deals for $4.2 billion, falling short of GV’s total by more than $1 billion.
Other major corporate VC actors in the pharma industry include Sanofi Ventures, which participated in 30 deals for a cumulative $3.7 billion, and Pfizer Ventures, which notched 18 deals for $1.3 billion.
Venture capital is the lifeblood of U.S. biopharma industry, with J.P. Morgan reporting that funding reached $23.9 billion across 385 rounds this year. Fundraisings have slowed in the third quarter but the bank predicts the trend will push 2026 to $33 billion, topping last year’s $30.5 billion.
