Mazda Launches 2027 CX-90 in the States, Crossover Is Basically the Same but a Bit Different
13 photos
Photo: Mazda
In production since 2023, the Mazda CX-90 has now entered the 2027 model year in the United States of America, where the company’s local branch has just announced the novelties and pricing details.
Since you probably want to find out what is new, we will start by telling you that the updated rear suspension bushings are part of the novelties, and these, together with the revised rear suspension crossmember, are said to deliver improved comfort over rough surfaces.
Four new exterior paint colors have also joined the palette, and these are called the Zircon Sand Metallic, Melting Copper Metallic, Navy Blue Mica, and Aero Grey Metallic. Last but not least, the 3.3 Turbo Premium Sport and the 3.3 Turbo S Premium Sport can now be configured with two rows of seats, making the CX-90 replace the CX-70 in the United States of America.
But what about the pricing, you ask? Well, the 2027 Mazda CX-90 now starts at $39,700 for the base 3.3 Turbo Select, which is $400 more than the equivalent 2026 model year grade. It features a 7-inch TFT display, a 10.25-inch infotainment system, an eight-speaker audio system, smartphone integration, push-button start, advanced keyless entry, a three-zone automatic climate control system, LED exterior lights, 19-inch wheels, and a few other things.
Photo: Mazda Power is supplied by a 3.3-liter turbocharged inline-six, which features 48-volt mild-hybrid assistance, and produces 280 hp (284 s/209 kW) and 332 lb-ft (450 Nm) of torque on 87-octane fuel. An eight-speed automatic transmission delivers everything to the standard i-Activ all-wheel drive system. Radar-guided cruise control with stop and go, blind spot monitoring, rear cross traffic alert, lane departure warning, driver attention alert, and other safety features are also on deck.
Mazda’s 2027 CX-90 3.3 Turbo Preferred is next, and starts at $43,850. It is also $400 more expensive over the previous model year, and adds stuff such as the 21-inch wheels, some piano black accents on the outside, roof rails, heated and ventilated front seats, heated second-row seating, an 8-way power-adjustable driver’s seat with power lumbar support and memory setting, an 8-way power-adjustable front passenger seat, a heated steering wheel, a 12.3-inch infotainment system, and a few other bits and bobs.
The 2026 3.3 Turbo Premium Sport version of the Mazda CX-90 used to start at $47,480, and can now be ordered from $46,880 for the 2027 model year with two rows of seats, or $48,080 with three rows. It can also be ordered with second-row captain’s chairs, and features different 21-inch wheels, some tweaks on the outside, piano black door mirror head covers, piano black roof rails, standard Alexa Built-In, and a few other things.
Mazda’s CX-90 3.3 Turbo Premium Plus comes next, carrying an MSRP of $50,670 for the 2027 model year, up from last year’s $50,270. It features more advanced headlights, Mazda Online Navigation with over-the-air updates, black or white Nappa leather upholstery, foot lamp illumination, and a 150-watt outlet in the cargo area. A 360-degree view monitor with see-through view and trailer hitch view, front cross traffic alert, and others are also on deck.
For the 2027 CX-90 PHEV Preferred, which features an electrified 2.5-liter naturally aspirated four-cylinder engine and a 17.8 kWh battery pack, and has 323 hp (327 ps/240 kW) and 369 lb-ft (500 Nm) of torque combined, you are looking at a minimum of $50,695, which is the same as the previous model year. It has an electric driving range of up to 27 miles (43 km), has Sport, Off-Road, and EV drive modes, 21-inch wheels, a power sunroof, a power tailgate, heated side mirrors, full LED lighting, rain-sensing wipers, etc.
Photo: Mazda Ventilated front seats, two-position memory for the driver’s seat, three-zone climate control, heated steering wheel, a 12.3-inch TFT LCD instrument panel display, a 12.3-inch infotainment system, wireless charging pads, more USB-C ports, wireless smartphone integration, front and rear parking sensors, and other stuff are also mentioned as being standard.
The PHEV Premium Sport version of the 2027 Mazda CX-90 comes from $55,500, which is also the same as before, and adds auto-dimming side mirrors with automatic power folding, a head-up display, a frameless and auto-dimming rearview mirror with HomeLink, a Bose sound system, and a few other features are also included here.
Mazda’s 2027 CX-90 PHEV Premium Plus starts at $58,700, unchanged from the previous model year, brings different 21-inch wheels, some tweaks on the outside, adaptive front lights, heated side mirrors with memory and tilt-down in reverse, Mazda Online Navigation, Nappa leather upholstery, and the usual safety gizmos, in addition to other stuff.
The 2027 Mazda CX-90 Turbo S Premium Sport, which packs an e-Skyactiv G 3.3-liter inline-six turbocharged engine, rated at 340 hp (345 ps/254 kW) and 369 lb-ft (488 Nm) of torque, starts at $53,540. It has Sport, Off-Road, and Towing modes, a blackout exterior theme, heated and ventilated seats, a heated steering wheel, black or white Nappa leather, etc. The 3.3 Turbo S Premium Plus kicks off at $57,970, and rounds off the offering with a bit more gear.

Joint Typhoon Warning Center
By Alison Koo
27 October 2026
Typhoon Champi and persistent congestion at major Southeast Asian and South Asian ports are providing temporary support to container freight rates, disrupting vessel schedules and delaying some ships by up to three days.
However, the reprieve is unlikely to reverse the market’s downward trajectory as excess capacity, aggressive price competition and the onset of the winter slack season continue to weigh on rates.
Linerlytica’s report today stated that Champi, declared the strongest storm of 2026 after making landfall in Taiwan on Saturday, has added to congestion in North Asia, which accounts for 35% of global port logjams.
Ahead of Champi’s arrival, Taiwan’s key ports Kaohsiung, Taipei and Keelung closed last Friday and resumed operations over the weekend.
The consultancy said: “Ports across Southeast and South Asia remain under pressure from vessel bunching. The situation is compounded by the return of some services through the Suez Canal, as ships resuming the shorter route converge with vessels still sailing around the Cape of Good Hope. These disruptions are temporarily absorbing effective capacity and offering some support to spot rates.”
Nevertheless, the underlying supply-demand imbalance remains unresolved, leaving carriers struggling to sustain pricing ahead of their planned 1 November GRI.
Linerlytica said: “Carriers’ plans for a GRI on 1 November are effectively doomed as the winter slack season kicks in, with the largest shipping lines undercutting each other.”
Last Friday, the Shanghai Containerised Freight Index showed Shanghai-North Europe rates were relatively unchanged from the previous week, at $3,557 per feu. Linerlytica though, noted that the reality on the ground was less rosy.
Gemini Cooperation partners Hapag-Lloyd and Maersk are offering some of the lowest spot rates for early November shipments, at $3,000–$3,200 per feu and $3,200–$3,400 per feu, respectively. MSC, Ocean Alliance and Premier Alliance carriers, have responded with offers of around $3,400–$3,500 per feu, suggesting carriers are prioritising securing cargo volumes over maintaining higher prices.
Carriers are maintaining full capacity deployments through November, with average weekly capacity from the Far East to North Europe expected to reach a record level. Capacity is also likely to remain elevated as carriers continue to resume Suez Canal transits, meaning shortened round voyages. Half of the Asia-North Europe sailings that were routed round the Cape of Good Hope in response to Houthi attacks have been returned to the Suez, with a full reversion expected in early 2027.

Garage Italia Spiaggina M Stretches the Fiat 500 Into a Proper Four-Seater
10 photos
Photo: Garage Italia
There are two major automotive events planned for early next month: the EICMA motorcycle show in Italy, and the SEMA show across the pond and one full continent away, in Las Vegas. With that in mind, very few people were paying attention to the trade show dedicated to vintage and classic cars taking place over the past weekend in Bordeaux, France.
It is from there that news of a new version of a vehicle called the Spiaggina reached us. Named, simply, M, it reinterprets the already reinterpreted Fiat 500 by adding an extra 6.7 inches (17 cm) of real estate, in a bid to make the four seats available genuinely comfortable.
That's the phrase the makers of the Spiaggina, a crew that goes by the name Garage Italia, use to describe the Spiaggina M newcomer, admitting that the base Fiat 500's legroom in the rear is not usually all that great.
The company added the extra inches at the rear of the Spiaggina, hoping that people will start using the vehicle for other activities, ranging from hospitality to longer pleasure journeys. In doing so, however, it didn't affect the rest of the car, nor did it modify its standard look.
To make sure that people do recognize it as a special car of its breed, Garage Italia gave the M a special paint job in Barolo metallic, which is, more or less, a shade of red, with contrasting Tellina (white) spread over the tubular structures and details.
All that is pulled over an interior in Mariaflora fabrics in red and white spread over the soft top, cushions, and the Alabastro seat produced by furniture company Bonacina 1889. Wrapping up the interior detailing are floor mats made so that their surface evokes natural fibers.
By trade, the Spiaggina is an electric vehicle conversion, and the same can be said about the recently presented M variant. Garage Italia does not go into the details of that, which means it packs the standard drivetrain we already know.
That would be electric motors that crank out just 13 hp and 82 Nm of torque, and a battery pack that promises a range of 87 miles (140 km). The car's top speed does not go over 47 mph (75 kph), but it doesn't really need to do that, seeing the way it is generally used.
The M version, however, does throw in something other Spiagginas don't usually get, and that is off-road tires, which, combined with the raised look of the design, makes the M look particularly potent.
This version also throws in a keyless entry system, dynamic power steering, and additional lights shielded by dedicated grilles.
The Italian company did not share the cost of the Spiaggina M , but don't imagine it to be cheap. After all, any Fiat 500 modified by Garage Italia and turned into the Spiaggina starts at a minimum of 85,000 euros, or $95,000 at today's exchange rates.

Novartis remains “very happy” with its $12 billion acquisition of Avidity Biosciences, despite a Phase 3 disappointment for the antibody-oligonucleotide conjugate del-desiran.
Novartis stands by its $12 billion takeover of Avidity Biosciences even after del-desiran, one of the main assets driving that buyout, failed a late-stage myotonic dystrophy study and spawned a $1.9 billion partial impairment charge.
“We remain very, very happy with the Avidity acquisition,” Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan told reporters during a Tuesday morning press call to present the pharma’s third quarter earnings results . “We feel confident that there’s a tremendous value we can still generate off of the platform and the three assets that we acquired.”
Narasimhan attributed the write-down to “the mathematical shift of our assumption.” Novartis still believes in the asset but has adjusted its valuation to account for the need to run an additional pivotal study, which will take time and money, he said.
Del-desiran is an antibody-oligonucleotide conjugate that targets transferrin receptor 1 on muscle cells and tags DMPK messenger RNA for destruction. Myotonic dystrophy type 1 is caused by mutations in the DMPK gene.
In September, data from the Phase 3 HARBOR study—which enrolled 159 patients with DM1 who were randomly assigned to del-desiran or placebo—showed that the investigational therapy failed to hit the study’s primary outcome of improving hand function.

The pharma plans to advance del-desiran into another pivotal program and is currently evaluating what the best path forward is, he added.
Narasimhan also emphasized the other clinical assets and the technology for antibody-oligonucleotide conjugates that Avidity brought to the Novartis fold. One of these candidates, called del-brax, is in Phase 3 development for facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy and for which the pharma is discussing with the FDA the potential for accelerated approval, Narasimhan said. Another Avidity asset, del-zota, has priority review for certain types of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
“So in our view, the Avidity acquisition remains absolutely on track,” Narasimhan said. “It’s hit a bump, which is normal, I think, when you’re trying to do pioneering science.”

Other bumps in Novartis’ quarter
Just a few days before the del-desiran announcement, the company reported that the antisense therapy pelacarsen failed to significantly lower cardiovascular risk in a late-stage trial. And these two disappointing readouts followed the news that Novartis had paused a host of mid-stage immunology and neurology studies for its CAR T therapy rapcabtagene autoleucel following three deaths.
These setbacks sent the pharma’s shares down some 13% in a week .
Narasimhan said on Tuesday’s call that while there have been no further safety events to report, those studies remain on hold in in U.S. and Europe. “It’s absolutely our goal to get these trials started again,” he said, highlighting the feedback the company has gotten from physicians and patients about the clinical benefits of these CAR T therapies. “We expect in the coming months to be able to provide further updates once we identify the root cause and also understand the best approach to ensure patient safety in the future.”

In the third quarter, Novartis reported net sales of $14.5 billion, up 4% year-over-year at constant currencies. The anti-inflammatory drug Cosentyx was Novartis’ top-selling drug for the third quarter with nearly $1.9 billion in earnings, up 9% from the same period last year.
Sales over the first nine months of the year hit $42 billion, flat versus the same period in 2025—though CFO Mukul Mehta pointed out during the press call that Novartis is “absorbing the largest patent expiry in our history.”
The pharma’s Entresto lost exclusivity in summer 2025 and faced immediate generic competition in the U.S. The chronic heart failure drug made $1.16 billion in the third quarter and $3.65 billion so far this year, down 38% and 45% in constant-currency since the same periods last year.
Novartis countered those decline with key growth drivers including the breast cancer drug Kisqali, which grew 37% since Q3 2025 to make $1.8 billion in the third quarter this year, and the multiple sclerosis medicine Kesimpta, which jumped 22% to hit $1.48 billion.

Earlier this month, Novartis ended a Phase 2 study for Fabhalta in lupus that has inflamed the kidneys. Aspokesperson said in an email to BioSpace that “the decision was based on strategic considerations and was not driven by any interim efficacy or safety findings.” Novartis will continue to study Fabhalta—which already has approvals in a rare blood disorder called paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria as well as IgA nephropathy and complement 3 glomerulopathy—in late-stage trials for atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome and generalized myasthenia gravis.

Artiva Biotherapeutics, which had been evaluating cell therapy AlloNK for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis and other autoimmune diseases, is exploring strategic options that could include dissolution and liquidation.
Following two patient deaths and questions about the clinical response durability of its lead candidate, Artiva Biotherapeutics is ending development of the asset, wiping out 94% of its workforce and exploring strategic options. Those options could include a merger, business combination, sale or licensing of assets, or dissolution and liquidation, the San Diego–based biotech announced Tuesday.
Artiva had 115 employees as of June 30, according to an SEC filing , meaning the layoffs could affect around 108 employees and leave the business with fewer than 10 people. The company expects to complete the workforce reduction in the first quarter of 2027, according to a Tuesday SEC filing .
The biotech’s actions, which include canning a planned Phase 3 pivotal trial, followed a risk-benefit review of AlloNK. Artiva was evaluating the allogeneic, off-the-shelf natural killer cell therapy in combination with rituximab in rheumatoid arthritis and other B-cell-driven conditions.
The two patient deaths were tied to a Phase 2a basket autoimmune disease trial, according to the announcement. One participant experienced a fatal neurological event following study treatment, which included protocol-specified lymphodepletion chemotherapy. Artiva did not disclose how long after dosing the fatality occurred. The investigator and an independent safety review determined the death was likely related to a chemotherapy-associated neurotoxicity. After Artiva reported the death to the FDA, the agency, investigators and a data safety monitoring board asked the company to pause enrollment and dosing in the study. The biotech also paused plans for Phase 3 trial enrollment and dosing.
The second patient death occurred two months after initiating the Phase 2a basket trial treatment. The investigator determined the fatality was unrelated to AlloNK or any other component of the treatment regimen, and a cause of death has not yet been determined. Artiva reported the death to the FDA, investigators and the data safety monitoring board.
In the biotech’s Tuesday announcement, Artiva also noted that updated clinical response data from patients receiving AlloNK in combination with rituximab continued to demonstrate deep B cell depletion and clinical activity consistent with previously reported findings. However, longer-term follow-up failed to show the level of clinical response durability the company required to support continued development.
Founded in 2019, Artiva raised $179 million in a 2024 upsized initial public offering. More recently, in August, the company announced it had raised $300 million with an underwritten offering in May and noted it was well capitalized to initiate and execute the planned Phase 3 trial. The biotech had cash, cash equivalents and investments of approximately $319.1 million as of Sept. 30. That was down from $349.1 million as of June 30.

Posted By: Colin McClelland October 27, 2026
Senior gold miners are trading almost a quarter below their five-year average valuation despite strong cash flow, as a selloff in precious metals shares extends into the fourth quarter, Haywood Securities says.
The producers trade at 6.82 times their expected cash flow over the next 12 months, compared with a five-year average of 8.83 times, Haywood’s mining analysis team said in a note on Tuesday. That puts the current multiple 23% below the historical average.
“We view the recent selloff as a period of consolidation within an ongoing bull market in precious metals,” Haywood said. “Key structural drivers including central bank accumulation, de-dollarization and elevated global debt levels remain in place.”
Haywood’s analysts expect near-term volatility as investors weigh high oil prices and inflation against the outlook for interest rates. Central bank buying, efforts to reduce reliance on the U.S. dollar and high global debt levels continue to support the longer-term case for precious metals, they say.
Gold index
Gold rose 3.7% in the third quarter, while the VanEck Gold Miners exchange-traded fund, known by its ticker GDX, returned 16%, according to Haywood. The metal gained 9.7% in August before falling 6.3% in September, with weakness continuing into the fourth quarter.
Spot gold climbed from about $4,009 per oz. earlier Tuesday to $4,022.74 at 9:15 a.m. in Toronto, ahead of the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision on Wednesday. The Fed is widely expected to hold its benchmark interest rate steady, although economists expect it to raise rates in December as inflation remains elevated. Higher interest rates can reduce the appeal of gold, which pays no interest.
The bank sees strong balance sheets supporting further mergers and acquisitions as producers seek to replenish reserves, increasing competition for exploration and development projects.
Haywood’s three top picks are First Mining Gold (TSX: FF), Thesis Gold & Silver (TSXV: TAU) and Troilus Mining (TSX: TLG), all Canadian developers.
First Mining Gold
At First Mining’s Springpole gold project in northwestern Ontario, Haywood expects a provincial environmental assessment decision in the near term. The project received federal approval for its environmental assessment in June.
First Mining shares closed 3.3% less at C58¢ apiece on Monday in Toronto, valuing the company at C$862 million ($614.6 million). Haywood rates the stock a buy with a C$1.75 target.
At Thesis’s Lawyers-Ranch gold-silver project in British Columbia’s Toodoggone district, Haywood expects a feasibility study before the end of 2027. Investments by Centerra Gold (TSX: CG) and AngloGold Ashanti (NYSE: AU), together with consolidation that has reduced the number of available Canadian development projects, could support Thesis’s valuation, the firm said.
Thesis shares closed 0.4% weaker at C$2.42 apiece on Monday, valuing the company a C$714 million. Haywood has a buy rating and a C$6.50 target.
In Quebec, Troilus is advancing its gold-copper project towards a construction decision after receiving a credit-approved commitment in September for $850 million (C$1.19 billion) of a planned $1.1-billion debt package. Final permits are expected in the first quarter of 2027, Haywood said.
Troilus shares closed 1.3% stronger at C$1.52 apiece on Monday in Toronto, valuing the company at C$843 million. Haywood rates the stock a buy with a C$4.50 target.
Metal prices
Haywood kept its forward commodity price assumptions unchanged in the latest update. It models gold at $4,000 per oz. in the fourth quarter and in 2027, rising to $4,250 in 2028 and $4,500 in 2029 and beyond.
For silver, the firm assumes $55 per oz. in the fourth quarter and in 2027, followed by $60 in 2028 and $65 in 2029 and beyond.
Gold averaged $4,263 per oz. in the third quarter, above Haywood’s $4,000 assumption but below the second-quarter average of $4,508. Silver averaged $62.71 per oz., above the firm’s $55 assumption and below the second-quarter average of $74.87.
The stronger-than-expected third-quarter prices lifted Haywood’s calculated annual averages to $4,411 per oz. for gold and $69.04 for silver, even though it left its fourth-quarter assumptions unchanged.

Antares Nuclear has secured a multi-year agreement with BWX Technologies (BWXT) for advanced nuclear fuel fabrication and received initial Department of Energy (DOE) safety approval for its Mark-1 microreactor, advancing two key requirements for the company’s planned transition from reactor testing to electricity production and military deployments.
The Torrance, California–based developer announced on Oct. 27 that BWXT Advanced Fuels will manufacture tri-structural isotropic (TRISO) fuel for its microreactors through the end of the decade, under an agreement that establishes terms for an initial allocation of one metric ton of uranium (MTU) and includes provisions to increase quantities as deployment requirements evolve.
The agreement comes on the heels of Antares’ Oct. 23 announcement that DOE had approved the Nuclear Safety Design Agreement (NSDA) for Mark-1, the company’s first electricity-producing reactor. Antares plans to operate Mark-1 at Idaho National Laboratory (INL) in 2027, ahead of initial deployments to U.S. military installations beginning in 2028.
Both developments build on the company’s June 4 achievement of zero-power criticality with its Mark-0 reactor, the first advanced reactor to reach that milestone under DOE’s Reactor Pilot Program. As POWER has reported, Mark-0 demonstrated a self-sustaining fission chain reaction but did not generate electricity. Mark-1, however, is intended to demonstrate sustained power production using a full-scale reactor core integrated with its heat-transfer and power-conversion systems, providing operating data to support Antares’ planned commercial reactor deployments.
BWXT Agreement Expands TRISO Fuel Supply Arrangements
Under the Oct. 27 agreement , BWXT will manufacture TRISO fuel at its Lynchburg, Virginia, facility, using the same fabrication line that supplied fuel for Antares’ Mark-0 reactor and the Department of War’s Project Pele transportable microreactor.
The agreement builds on BWXT’s existing manufacturing relationship with Antares, extending fuel production arrangements to support the company’s planned transition from reactor demonstrations to initial production deployments. However, specific quantities, delivery schedules, and technical requirements remain subject to subsequent task orders as Antares’ reactor program progresses, BWXT said, and it did not disclose financial terms.
“We achieved criticality with BWXT fuel, and it’s what will power our electricity-producing reactor, Mark-1, in 2027,” said Jordan Bramble, Antares’ CEO and co-founder. “Securing that same line through the end of the decade means our first production deployments run on fuel from a team and a process we’ve already proven.”
TRISO fuel consists of uranium-bearing kernels surrounded by successive layers of carbon and ceramic materials, including silicon carbide, designed to retain fission products under high temperatures and irradiation. Antares’ reactors use high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU), containing less than 20% uranium-235, fabricated into TRISO fuel compacts. The fuel’s ability to retain fission products at elevated temperatures is a key feature of several advanced reactor designs, including compact, high-temperature microreactors.
“BWXT’s decades of experience in advanced fuel manufacturing give us the foundation to support Antares as they accelerate toward commercial deployment,” said Joe Miller, president of BWXT Government Operations. “Our team has refined the processes for high-performance TRISO fuel, and this agreement enables us to apply those strengths in a sustained, predictable way. As demand grows across the advanced reactor sector, BWXT is prepared to scale.”
The BWXT arrangement marks Antares’ second TRISO fuel fabrication agreement. In August, the developer signed a binding agreement with Standard Nuclear covering a minimum of 1 MTU and up to 8 MTU in total, with deliveries extending through 2035. Standard Nuclear, which is expanding its TRISO manufacturing operations, said the agreement would support Antares’ microreactors for defense and space applications.
Notably, the fabrication agreements complement separate arrangements to secure HALEU enrichment services and material supply, addressing different stages of the nuclear fuel supply chain. Although TRISO fabrication involves manufacturing coated fuel particles and finished fuel forms, developers must also secure the enriched uranium feedstock needed for production, making access to qualified fabrication capacity and enrichment services distinct requirements for reactor deployment.
In September, Antares and Centrus Energy announced a definitive multi-year HALEU supply contract , with deliveries expected to begin before the end of the decade. The agreement includes prepayments from Antares to support Centrus’ expansion of domestic enrichment capacity at its American Centrifuge Plant in Piketon, Ohio, where the company is pursuing commercial-scale production of HALEU and conventional low-enriched uranium.
The companies said the arrangement could provide U.S.-origin, “unobligated” HALEU suitable for national security applications, including defense and space missions. The designation is significant because nuclear material produced under certain international agreements may be subject to restrictions on its use, whereas unobligated material can support eligible U.S. national security missions.
“Fuel supply is one of the practical questions every advanced reactor developer has to answer,” Bramble said in the September announcement. “This contract gives Antares a reliable, U.S.-origin source of HALEU for the reactors we’re deploying for a wide variety of defense and space customers.”
Antares has also established HALEU supply arrangements with Urenco and General Matter, broadening its prospective sourcing options as it prepares for deployments beyond its initial demonstration program. However, the agreements represent different stages of fuel procurement and production, and their announced quantities and timelines should not be interpreted as confirmation that finished fuel for all planned reactor deployments has already been manufactured or delivered.
Mark-1 Moves Through DOE Authorization
Meanwhile, DOE’s approval of Mark-1’s NSDA marks the first formal step in the reactor’s safety authorization process, establishing design requirements, the safety analysis approach, and regulatory expectations that will govern the project through construction and operation.
According to Antares’ Oct. 23 announcement , Mark-1 will use the same full-scale core, TRISO fuel, and INL test facility as Mark-0, but will incorporate the company’s nitrogen closed Brayton-cycle power-conversion system. Antares plans to operate Mark-1 at full electrical power in 2027, targeting a six-month operating campaign intended to generate data on the integrated reactor system.
The company’s underlying R1 design uses a TRISO-fueled prismatic graphite core and passive sodium heat pipes to transport heat to a primary heat exchanger, where thermal energy is transferred to a nitrogen working fluid for electricity generation. As POWER previously reported , the design incorporates a recuperated nitrogen closed Brayton cycle operating at less than 300 psi, reflecting Antares’ emphasis on a compact, transportable system intended for long-duration operation.
Mark-0, however, was configured specifically for zero-power testing and was not equipped with power-conversion or heat-removal systems. Its principal objectives included validating reactor physics, reactivity control, and the safety authorization process. Mark-1 will extend that testing to sustained thermal and electrical operation, allowing Antares to evaluate temperature-dependent reactor effects, reactivity feedback, and the coupled behavior of the reactor core and power-conversion system. The planned campaign will also test whether the integrated system can maintain stable operating conditions over an extended period, which is an important requirement for the company’s intended military applications.
Notably, Antares has also pursued non-nuclear testing of electrically heated demonstration units at its Antares Prime facility in Torrance, including a second testing campaign in 2026 incorporating an updated heat-pipe design and control system. The parallel testing program allows the company to evaluate thermal components, inspect materials between test runs, and refine aspects of the heat-transfer and power-conversion systems independently of nuclear operations.
“Mark-0 proved we could take a reactor from a paper design to a self-sustaining chain reaction on the timeline we promised,” Bramble said in the Oct. 23 announcement. “Mark-1 isn’t a scaled-down, stand-in test rig. It’s commercially representative of the plant we’ll deploy to Fort Bragg under the Army Janus program in 2028. Mark-1 will be the first full-scale electricity-producing microreactor test in the United States. Operating at full electrical power for six months gives us comprehensive test data on every major subsystem and how they behave together. DOE’s approval of this safety agreement is the gate that lets us move not only from neutrons to electrons, but to customer plants, on schedule.”
The NSDA approval, however, does not authorize reactor operation, and Antares must complete additional safety reviews and obtain subsequent DOE approvals before Mark-1 can begin its planned operating campaign. The company followed a similar authorization sequence for Mark-0, securing NSDA approval in October 2025, Preliminary Documented Safety Analysis approval in January 2026, and Documented Safety Analysis approval in April before achieving criticality in June.
DOE’s authorization process for testing at INL is also separate from the regulatory requirements governing deployment at military installations, where Antares must address applicable site-specific safety, environmental, and operational considerations as it pursues its targeted 2028 deployments.
Separately, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) on Oct. 22 finalized a rule allowing commercial reactor applicants to reference prior DOE- and military-authorized reactor demonstrations when demonstrating compliance with NRC safety requirements. Published in the Federal Register on Oct. 26, the rule amends 10 CFR Parts 50 and 53 to explicitly permit consideration of relevant information from federally authorized reactors that have been tested and demonstrated the ability to function safely. The provisions could eventually allow developers such as Antares to reference prior authorization and testing information in future commercial reactor licensing applications, although Antares has not announced plans to pursue NRC licensing for Mark-1. Applicants must demonstrate how the information satisfies applicable NRC requirements, including accounting for differences between previously authorized reactor designs and proposed commercial configurations, while the NRC retains responsibility for independently reviewing each application.
Non-nuclear testing equipment at Antares Nuclear’s Antares Prime facility in Torrance, California, where the company is developing heat-transfer systems and preparing its Mark-1 microreactor for a planned electricity-producing demonstration in 2027. Following an Oct. 21 visit by senior Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) officials, Antares said it “recognizes the value of early and sustained pre-application engagement with the NRC,” adding that such engagement is “foundational to a predictable, efficient licensing process” as it advances toward commercial microreactor deployment. Courtesy: Antares Nuclear
Testing Supports 2028 Military Deployment Plans
The planned Mark-1 demonstration is intended to support development of Antares’ R1 microreactor, a modular, transportable unit rated at 100 kWe to 1 MWe and designed to operate for six or more years between refueling. The reactor’s architecture incorporates passive heat transport, a compact power-conversion system, and an integrated transport cradle that includes shielding, reflecting the company’s focus on providing long-duration power for defense applications.
According to technical details previously reported by POWER , the R1 also includes a power management and distribution node designed to connect directly to installation microgrids, potentially allowing military facilities to maintain an independent electricity supply without continuous reliance on the commercial grid. Antares has emphasized reliability, uptime, and manufacturability in the design, rather than maximizing power density.
Antares’ most immediate deployment target is Fort Bragg in North Carolina, where the U.S. Army selected the company in August under its $2.2 billion Janus Program. That initiative seeks to deploy more than 20 commercial microreactors across military installations, beginning with five selected developers and sites. Antares plans to deploy three R1 microreactors at Fort Bragg, each rated at between 100 kWe and 1 MWe. As POWER reported in detail , the Army’s initial Janus agreements use fixed-price, milestone-based Other Transaction Authority contracts, under which participating developers must complete specified technical and deployment milestones to receive government payments. The contracting structure is intended to manage development and execution risks while advancing multiple reactor technologies toward operation at military installations.
The company is also pursuing a prototype deployment at Joint Base San Antonio, Texas, under the Department of the Air Force’s Advanced Nuclear Power for Installations initiative, which selected Antares in April 2026. That effort involves a separate regulatory pathway from the DOE-authorized test program at INL and remains subject to applicable environmental reviews and regulatory approvals.
Beyond terrestrial defense applications, Antares is developing reactor technology for space missions. In September, the company announced its selection for a $161 million Space Force Strategic Breakthrough award to advance its R1-S space reactor through a nuclear ground demonstration and spacecraft integration activities intended to support flight certification. Antares has also said its planned Mark-1 operating campaign will support an operational ground-to-space asset, extending the demonstration’s potential applications beyond military installation power.

DOE’s authorization process for testing at INL is also separate from the regulatory requirements governing deployment at military installations, where Antares must address applicable site-specific safety, environmental, and operational considerations as it pursues its targeted 2028 deployments.

Separately, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) on Oct. 22 finalized a rule allowing commercial reactor applicants to reference prior DOE- and military-authorized reactor demonstrations when demonstrating compliance with NRC safety requirements.

Published in the Federal Register on Oct. 26, the rule amends 10 CFR Parts 50 and 53 to explicitly permit consideration of relevant information from federally authorized reactors that have been tested and demonstrated the ability to function safely.

The provisions could eventually allow developers such as Antares to reference prior authorization and testing information in future commercial reactor licensing applications, although Antares has not announced plans to pursue NRC licensing for Mark-1.

Following an Oct. 21 visit by senior Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) officials, Antares said it “recognizes the value of early and sustained pre-application engagement with the NRC,” adding that such engagement is “foundational to a predictable, efficient licensing process” as it advances toward commercial microreactor deployment.

That initiative seeks to deploy more than 20 commercial microreactors across military installations, beginning with five selected developers and sites.
Antares plans to deploy three R1 microreactors at Fort Bragg, each rated at between 100 kWe and 1 MWe.

As POWER reported in detail , the Army’s initial Janus agreements use fixed-price, milestone-based Other Transaction Authority contracts, under which participating developers must complete specified technical and deployment milestones to receive government payments.

The company is also pursuing a prototype deployment at Joint Base San Antonio, Texas, under the Department of the Air Force’s Advanced Nuclear Power for Installations initiative, which selected Antares in April 2026.

In September, the company announced its selection for a $161 million Space Force Strategic Breakthrough award to advance its R1-S space reactor through a nuclear ground demonstration and spacecraft integration activities intended to support flight certification.

Man Buys New 2025 Rolls-Royce Spectre for $468,375, Drives 1,800 Miles, Sells for $360,000
22 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
The only thing worse than offering up your services and your wallet as an early adopter for EV tech is doing it when it comes to a very expensive luxury product. Since new, this 2025 Rolls-Royce Spectre has probably lost nearly $100,000 per year in depreciation, which means that in another couple of years, it's going to be a $200,000 car at best, depending on mileage.
Then you need to figure out the long term prospects when it comes to Spectre ownership. How much will this be worth 10 years from now? Less than a new i7 or Taycan? Conceivably. Although, for somebody looking for that Rolls-Royce experience, a used Spectre could make a great deal of sense. Yet, talking about such a car from the buyer's perspective seems a little too "on the nose". You've got to be hurting if you're the seller.
Again, with this Spectre in particular (a 2025MY car), the original MSRP stood at $468,375. The car was delivered new to the seller via Rolls-Royce Rancho Mirage in California, and driven only 1,800 miles before getting sold at auction for $360,000. Five years from now, this thing is going to be worth less than a Patek. Heck, it's already there, depending on which wristwatch model we're talking about.
So yeah, who could have known that in terms of depreciation, the Spectre would suffer the same fate as the Lucid Air ? This guy right here (I'm raising my hand), that's who. The range is borderline acceptable and so are the charge times (if you have access to DC fast charging), but those numbers are only getting worse with time. Its battery tech is already inferior to that of the Bentley Torcal, which is cheaper, faster and obviously more powerful.
But enough of that. I feel like I'm being a little mean so let's focus on some of the positives - like the spec of this car. Aside from the Black Diamond colorway, other noteworthy features include the adaptive LED headlights, a surround camera system, power-assisted coach doors, 23" seven-spoke wheels with self-leveling RR center emblems, Pirelli P Zero rubber, adaptive air suspension, active rear-axle steering, and more.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Meanwhile, interior highlights include the Phoenix Red and black perforated leather upholstery, Piano Black veneers, ventilated and massaging front seats, a black Shooting Star leather headliner, red leather door panels with Starlight illumination, quad-zone climate control, lambswool floor mats, black and red umbrellas, a head-up display, leather-wrapped steering wheel, and a 415-watt, 16-speaker Premium Audio sound system.
As for performance, you get a dual-motor AWD setup putting down 577 horsepower and 660 lb-ft (900 Nm) of torque. It can get you from zero to 60 mph (97 kph) in about 4.4 seconds, with an EPA range of 251-277 miles. Or up to 530 km if we're talking WLTP figures.
It goes without saying that all those numbers look better in the Spectre Series II , which was unveiled earlier this year. It's got 18% more range to go with a 14% reduction in charging times. But rest assured that it'll go down in value just as rapidly as the original.

Double Nickel has launched an artificial intelligence agent to automate employment verifications for trucking companies, targeting a time-consuming part of driver recruiting and regulatory compliance.
The New York-based company said Thursday, Oct. 22, that its Vera agent completed 40% of employment verifications autonomously during beta testing. Two trucking carriers with more than 500 trucks between them tested the product over the last 30 days. During that period, Vera attempted about 250 verifications and autonomously completed more than 100, according to the company.
Verifications completed by Vera took an average of one day, compared with four days for manual verifications handled through Double Nickel’s applicant tracking system, according to the company. Vera costs $7 per verified employment experience, Double Nickel said. The company charges customers only when a verification is completed.
The agent identifies contacts at a driver’s previous employers, sends verification requests and follows up by phone and email . It also records and transcribes calls and logs its attempts. Double Nickel said Vera identifies itself as a virtual assistant and informs call recipients that the line is recorded. The company said consent to recording is collected during the application process through its applicant tracking system, where Vera operates.
Obtaining the information can require recruiting or safety staff to locate the right contact at a former employer, send requests and follow up when responses are delayed. If contact information is missing, Vera can call the former employer to obtain it and save the details for future requests, Double Nickel said.
When Vera cannot complete a verification, it helps carriers document their attempts to contact the previous employer, according to the company. Vera may be unable to complete a verification automatically if a former employer has closed, does not respond to its requests or uses a third-party platform the agent does not yet support, Double Nickel said. In those cases, carriers may need to handle the verification themselves or document their attempts to obtain the information. The company said it is working to support additional platforms.
Vera is now available to all Double Nickel customers.
Federal rules
The launch addresses a process governed by federal regulations requiring motor carriers to investigate the safety performance histories of prospective drivers who worked for other Department of Transportation -regulated employers during the previous three years.
Under 49 CFR 391.23, carriers must investigate a driver’s employment history and safety performance, including relevant crash records and certain drug and alcohol violations. Carriers generally must obtain the required information or document their good-faith efforts within 30 days of the driver’s first day of service. The records must be maintained as part of the driver’s qualification file.
The federal Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse , which launched in January 2020, has centralized records of drug and alcohol violations for commercial driver’s license holders. Since January 2023, employers have been required to query the Clearinghouse as part of pre-employment checks rather than relying on previous employers for those records. However, carriers must still investigate other required aspects of a driver’s employment and safety history, including applicable crash records and safety performance information.
“Fleets we talk to consistently tell us that employment verifications remain one of the most manual, time-consuming parts of the driver hiring process,” Francisco López Roualdes, CEO and co-founder of Double Nickel said.
Carriers remain responsible for meeting federal driver investigation and recordkeeping requirements when using outside services. The FMCSA says motor carriers must retain safety performance history records for the duration of a driver’s employment and three years afterward.
Why this matters
Driver employment verifications can delay hiring as carriers wait for former employers to provide records. Automating the process could reduce administrative workloads and help carriers move drivers through recruiting faster, though Vera’s 40% autonomous completion rate suggests human involvement remains necessary for many verifications. Carriers also remain responsible for meeting federal requirements when using automated tools.

Superyacht Concept Project White Arrow Is Designed To Be a Luxurious Floating Sanctuary
6 photos
Photo: Nuvolari Lenard
As modern superyacht owners are looking for vessels that can serve as more than just luxurious holiday escapes, designers are finding ways to create concepts envisioned from the get-go as private floating residences, designed to make life on the water more comfortable, personal, and enjoyable.
Nuvolari Lenard, one of the most active and renowned yacht design firms in the world, has unveiled a new superyacht concept aimed specifically at this new generation of owners. It’s called Project White Arrow and blurs the line between a watercraft for maritime exploration and a luxury floating home.
A 116-meter (380-foot) behemoth, this new yacht concept is designed for seafarers who want to live full-time at sea, with generous living quarters, modern wellness facilities, and a setting meant to facilitate a deeper connection with the surrounding ocean.
Developed in collaboration with Florida-based brokerage and yacht management firm Moran Yacht & Ship, White Arrow builds on Nuvolari’s heritage while also taking into consideration current trends and the desires of future owners.
The vessel is presented as a ready-to-build project, but instead of offering a finished, fixed design, it’s more of a starting point, allowing future owners to tailor its architecture, interior design, and onboard features to their tastes and needs, with a focus on the quality of the onboard experience .
Photo: Nuvolari Lenard “Project White Arrow reflects this changing ‘sentiment’, exploring how scale, architecture and design can create an environment that feels both exceptional and deeply liveable,” declared studio co-founder Carlo Nuvolari. “A yacht of this scale gives you an extraordinary opportunity, but also a responsibility: to create something that feels coherent, effortless and ultimately human.”
The owner can also choose the shipyard responsible for bringing the concept to life. That’s why the design firm explains the project was “conceived to explore the next generation of bespoke design.”
From the renderings revealed so far, Project White Arrow shapes up as an imposing superyacht with a sculptural profile. Its exterior is defined by long, uninterrupted lines, a plumb bow, and expansive glazing. An elongated foredeck and cascading aft decks create a sleek silhouette, while large stretches of glazing provide a close connection with the surrounding sea.
One of the project’s highlights is the aft deck, which is fitted with a glass-fronted swimming pool that extends above the beach club and swim platform, allowing outdoor relaxation and access to the water to intertwine. The expansive beach club leads to a wellness center with a sauna, steam room, two massage rooms and a full-beam gym with views across the water.
Project White Arrow is also envisioned with a winter garden with a working firepit, providing another space for gathering and relaxation, as well as a full-size pickleball court.
Photo: Nuvolari Lenard With a beam of almost 17 feet (5.2 meters), the superyacht offers 5,200 GT of interior volume. This means plenty of space for creating sprawling living quarters. And since the idea was to create a “home on the water,” the interior layout is designed to support extended stays, with nine staterooms and dedicated areas for privacy and common living.
The owner will benefit from an entire deck, complete with a private lounge, and there will also be accommodation for 40 crew members.
Other luxurious modern features that will be present onboard include a helipad, garage space for four tenders, and water toys for recreational activities beyond the yacht itself.
In terms of power, the yacht is set to feature a hybrid diesel-electric propulsion system, though no further details have been revealed yet.
All in all, Project White Arrow represents Nuvolari Lenard’s interpretation of a broader shift in how modern owners approach life at sea, with comfort, privacy, wellness and flexibility playing increasingly more important roles. But ultimately, the client will have the opportunity to put their own stamp on the yacht’s design and onboard experience.
“The most interesting projects are not necessarily those that arrive with every answer already defined,” concludes Dan Lenard. “They are the ones that establish a strong vision and leave the right space for the owner to make it their own.”

Across the east-west container trades in August and September, MSC achieved reliability of 68.9%, narrowly ahead of the Gemini Cooperation at 68.4%, according to Sea-Intelligence.
The result marks a reversal for Gemini partners Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd as their reliability fell 9.4 percentage points, month on month, to 68.4%. Although Maersk proved the most reliable individual carrier on the trades.
MSC also declined, but by a more modest 1.2 percentage points, allowing it to take the lead.
The performance remained well short of Gemini’s stated ambition of around 90% reliability, although performance varied significantly by trade.
According to recent Sea-Intelligence data, Gemini maintained strong reliability on several routes, including Asia-North Europe, where it did achieve 92.9%, compared with MSC’s 78.2%. And on Asia-Mediterranean, Gemini achieved 83.2%, against MSC’s 77.1%.
Industry consultant Lara Jensen noted that for Gemini, the overall “low performance” was particularly driven by the backhaul trades from North America and Europe to Asia. And he added: “And is hence likely a consequence of the typhoon-induced issues in Far East ports.”
The transatlantic, however, remained a particular strength for Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd, achieving reliability of 98.7% on North America East Coast-Mediterranean, and 97% on North America East Coast-North Europe. On the westbound transatlantic, reliability reached 100% on Mediterranean-North America East Coast and 91.1% on North Europe-North America East Coast.
But Gemini’s performance was dragged down by an overall decline across the east-west network, with MSC proving more resilient.
Industry-wide, schedule reliability on the east-west trades fell 3.5 percentage points month on month, to 53.6% in August and September. The Ocean Alliance achieved reliability of 44.8%, down 3.4 percentage points, while the Premier Alliance declined 1.5 points, to 41.5%.
The latest figures continue persistently weak container shipping schedule reliability. Across the 13 largest carriers, reliability edged up by just 0.9 percentage points in September, to 50.6%, following three consecutive monthly declines that wiped 14.8 percentage points off the May peak of 64.5%.
Average delay for late vessel arrivals improved by 0.3 days, to 6.65 days, but remained the second-highest September figure on record, according to Sea-Intelligence.
Maersk was the most reliable individual carrier last month, at 64.8%, followed by Hapag-Lloyd, at 60.4%. MSC recorded 57.7%, while CMA CGM reached 51.8%.
None of the 13 carriers improved their reliability compared with September 2025. Zim saw the smallest decline, at 8.7 percentage points, while Pacific International Lines (PIL) suffered the largest, 27.3 points.
Sea-Intelligence also found that on-time performance diverged sharply across individual tradelanes. Reliability on Asia-North America west coast fell 7.1 percentage points month on month, to 53.5%, while Asia-North America east coast dropped 8.6 points, to 53%.
East coast South America-Asia saw the largest monthly decline across the 34 lanes monitored, falling 11 percentage points, to just 28.2%. By contrast, Europe-Oceania reliability improved 7.5 points, to 74.2%.
The figures underline the gap between alliance-level ambitions and the operational performance shippers are experiencing. Although Gemini continues to deliver high reliability on selected European and transatlantic routes, MSC’s stronger overall result highlights the challenge of maintaining consistent schedules across a global network.

This BMW X5 M Was Over $120K New, Just Sold for Less Than Half After 43,500 Miles
15 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Depreciation tends to hit some cars like a freight train. Take this 2022 model year BMW X5 M Competition , for instance, which just sold for less than half the money it cost its first owner a few years ago.
As mentioned above, it is a 2022 model year machine, which was $120,695 new, according to the attached window sticker. How much do you think it went for? Normally, we would have kept this information close to our chest until the end of the story, but we’ll make an exception this time. The number was $55,000.
The crossover was advertised at the excitement of no reserve at an online auction on Cars&Bids that ended on October 26, 2026, and it found a new home for itself quite easily, proving that you don’t have to break the bank in order to own a modern performance-oriented machine. In fact, it cost less than a new Toyota Land Cruiser , which requires spending a minimum of $58,180, before destination, options, and dealer fees.
And if you think that the mileage is in the six-digit territory, then you clearly haven’t paid attention to the title, because this 2022 BMW X5 M Competition had a decent 43,500 miles (70,000 km) on the clock at the time of cataloging. It has a clean North Carolina title, and is still located in Charlotte, though not for long, because it will soon be on its way to its new owner.
Photo: Cars&Bids The vehicle has a Black Sapphire Metallic exterior paint finish beneath the matte blue vinyl wrap, which is said to have been applied some two years ago, and should be removed within five to seven years, according to the seller. Other modifications include the leather and Alcantara-wrapped steering wheel, the paddle shifters with capacitive touch bypass, and a RaceChip GTS Black tuning module.
As a result, this BMW X5 M could produce a bit more power compared to the standard one. However, we do not know the numbers, because a dyno chart was not supplied. With zero outside intervention, the twin-turbocharged 4.4-liter V8 engine develops 617 hp (460 kW/625 ps) and 553 lb-ft (750 Nm) of torque, with the peak torque available at 1,800-5,800 rpm, and the maximum output at 6,000 rpm.
The twin-turbocharged V8 engine rockets this model from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) in just 3.9 seconds, and up to an electronically limited top speed of 155 mph (250 kph). With the optional M Driver’s Pack, the maximum speed increases to 180 mph (290 kph). An eight-speed automatic transmission delivers everything to the xDrive all-wheel drive system
Stuff such as the M Competition Package, Executive Package, Competition Package 2, and Drivers Assistance Pro Package are mentioned in the ad, alongside the heated front and rear seats, ventilated and massaging front seats, and 21-inch wheels at the front, and 22-inch wheels at the rear.
But what about the known flaws, you ask? Well, these include some chips in the windshield and on the hood, scratches on the wheels , scuffs on the driver’s door card, creases on the driver’s seat, and some scratches and pinholes in the vinyl wrap. Moreover, this BMW X5 M is said to have sustained “minor” damage to its right side two years ago, in October 2024.
Photo: Cars&Bids The service history reveals that the engine oil and filter were changed in January 2026, at 35,736 miles (57,512 km), and that the sunroof seal, dashboard, front passenger seat bottom leather, and front windshield washer pump strainer were replaced in June 2025, at 31,440 miles (50,598 km). The four tires were replaced, mounted, and balanced in January 2025, at 27,162 miles (43,713 km), and that is also when the rear brake pads were replaced, and the engine oil and filter were changed.
Additional service entries are also mentioned in the ad, which shows that the BMW X5 M in question is accompanied by the factory steering wheel, the OEM paddle shifters and touch sensor module, a flat tire kit, the owner’s manual, and two keys. The seller claims to have bought the super crossover from a dealer in January 2025, adding some 16,400 miles (26,400 km) since.
Now, we already told you how much this 2022 BMW X5 M Competition went for, but how much is one of these in today’s used car market in the States? Depending on the usual factors, that would be between $50,000 and roughly $75,000. High-mileage examples can dip below $50K, and low-mileage ones, with less than 30,000 miles (48,000 km) on their odometers, featuring plenty of gear, can pull close to the $70,000 mark.
Therefore, in theory, this BMW X5 M should have gone for more than $55,000, which was the selling price, but how much would it have been worth in your opinion? The listing can be accessed here on the quoted website.

The device is designed to help logistics operators maintain visibility into trailers, shipping containers and other equipment in areas with limited network coverage, with commercial availability planned for early 2027. Selected participants are expected to receive their devices in December, though Band24 has not set an exact delivery date.
The company announced Terra on Oct. 6, saying it can track asset location, movement, dwell time, temperature, humidity and tampering. Band24 has opened an early-access program, with selected participants expected to receive devices in December.
“Every business with physical assets has felt this same pain — you can see your equipment until the exact moment it matters most, and then it’s gone dark,” Band24 co-founder and CEO Patrick Patel said in the announcement.
The launch comes as cargo theft continues to be a problem . Verisk’s CargoNet recorded 2,646 confirmed cargo thefts across the United States and Canada in 2025, an 18% increase from 2024. Estimated losses reached nearly $725 million, up 60%, while the average value per theft climbed to $273,990.
Combining three networks
Terra combines Bluetooth, LTE-M cellular and satellite connectivity through Hubble Network’s low-Earth-orbit satellite network.
The device is designed to use a terrestrial Bluetooth network of more than 100 million crowdsourced access points for routine updates and location determination, LTE-M cellular connectivity when coverage is available, and Hubble’s satellite network when the other two networks are unavailable. Hubble’s satellite technology allows Bluetooth Low Energy devices to send small data packets directly to passing satellites using their existing Bluetooth radios, without requiring a dedicated satellite modem.
Band24 says Terra can return an on-demand location update in about a minute when cellular or terrestrial Bluetooth connectivity is available. Outside those networks, the device relies on satellite transmissions when a Hubble satellite passes overhead, meaning updates follow the satellite’s schedule rather than an on-demand clock. Band24 said satellite performance is expected to improve as Hubble expands its constellation. Hubble reported six satellites in low-Earth orbit as of Sept. 23, 2026.
Terra determines location using a combination of GPS, Wi-Fi localization and a terrestrial network of more than 100 million crowdsourced Bluetooth access points, according to Band24. Hubble’s satellite network provides coarse location information when other methods are unavailable. The device selects when to report and which network to use based on factors including LTE availability, nearby Bluetooth access points and sensor inputs.
The distinction between on-demand and satellite reporting could matter to fleet operators that need to locate equipment quickly in remote areas. Band24 has not provided location-accuracy figures or data on satellite reporting reliability.
Testing and performance
Terra remains in testing and development as Band24 works through regulatory certification ahead of commercial shipment.
Band24 estimates the device’s battery life at four years, though the company said measurements are ongoing and the estimate remains directional. It attributes the expected battery life to its multi-network strategy, which selects a power-efficient connection for each update, low-power wireless technology and on-demand reporting that allows the device to remain inactive between check-ins.
The enclosure carries an IP68 rating for dust and water resistance. Terra will connect to Band24’s existing Ranger dashboard and Events API, and users will be able to activate and assign devices using an NFC-enabled smartphone.
Pricing and availability
Band24 has not announced Terra’s hardware price or subscription costs, saying it plans to share pricing closer to general availability. The device will be licensed per unit and will not require customers to purchase hubs or build private networks. The company expects its combination of three connectivity options and multi-year battery life to be competitively priced, but has not provided figures for comparing its total cost with existing trackers.
Why this matters
Freight operators often have limited visibility into trailers, containers and other equipment when they move beyond cellular coverage or between facilities. Terra aims to address those gaps by combining Bluetooth, cellular and satellite connectivity in a single battery-powered tracker. Its value for the logistics industry will depend on whether satellite reporting is frequent and reliable enough to locate assets when needed, as well as the device’s cost and battery life compared with existing tracking options.

By Ian Putzger Americas correspondent
27 October 2026
Faced with existential cost challenges, perishables shippers have welcomed the initiative of the Global Coalition of Fresh Produce (GCFP) to improve logistics flows through a charter of best practices – but some industry executives want better metrics to track carrier performance in order to make significant headway.
The GCFP’s latest survey, published last week, shows an industry in distress; where many operators are struggling with rising costs – from fuel and shipping over fertiliser to plant protection products and packaging, with 85% reporting higher costs in each of these categories.
Nearly two-thirds of respondents saw costs rise 10% or more, and one in seven reported increases in excess of 50%. Most struggle to pass the higher costs on to customers, and almost two-thirds consider their medium-term economic sustainability threatened.
At the Fruit Attraction event in Madrid this month, the GCFP unveiled its charter of best practices, which aims for a collaborative approach by all participants in produce supply chains. ( See Produce shippers prepare best practice charter for transport – The Loadstar )
It espouses collaboration and communication, fair and transparent business terms, competition and efficiency, cargo integrity and product quality, supported by optimal handling, resilience, and risk preparedness.
The charter was well received at the event, but some found it did not go far enough to bring about a transformative change. Edouard Brière, founder of Trackberry, a container tracking and document automation platform for fresh produce importers, called it “a welcome step forward”, but added that it needed importer-focused measurements to succeed.
He highlighted ocean carrier schedule reliability, arguing that ETA at destination port was a metric that missed the impact of schedule changes on the importer. Whether or not a vessel arrived technically on time is irrelevant if the imported container is not ready to move at the time the importer planned – be it due to schedule updates during transit, late arrival of documentation, or other factors.
To a large extent, the problem lies in communication, he believes.
“The recurrent frustration [for importers] is not that a ship is late. It’s that they find out too late to do anything about it,” Mr Brière added.
He pointed out that failure to have the container ready to go as planned rapidly piled up costs for importers – for storage at the port and electricity to power the reefer, for a wasted truck journey and warehouse costs. However, these pale in comparison to penalties for missing deadlines buyers set to sell the produce during a planned window, and lost business down the road.
What matters to the importer is how close the arrival was to the arrival estimated a week ahead, how often that estimate changed, how late the importer was informed about this, and whether or not the documents required for clearing the shipment arrived ahead of the cargo, he argued.
According to him, measuring carrier reliability should not be difficult for the GCFP. All that would be needed is a container number and its promised departure and arrival dates, he suggested, adding that importers could track shipments per lane and carrier to monitor how expected time of arrival strays from the schedule they had been given.

When Spartan Carrier Group founder and CEO Carlos M. Llanes Jr. started digging into artificial intelligence two years ago, his team did not buy it. Today the Fort Worth, Texas-based carrier’s vice president of operations is learning to build AI agents himself.
Spartan grew from zero trucks to about 150 in five years hauling just-in-time automotive freight, with Toyota as its biggest customer. It wants to keep growing with the staff it has. Its first AI agent builds the hourly customer reports that dispatchers had been making by hand. Its second, aimed at driver payroll, has not been tested yet.
Alvys launched Foundry in August to let carriers build AI agents inside its transportation management system , and named Spartan as an early customer.
Kendrick Dawson, who joined Spartan from Ryder in 2021 and is now its vice president of operations, was one of the doubters when Llanes first made his case.
“At the time, all of us looked at him like he was absolutely insane,” Dawson told FreightWaves in an interview at Trimble Insight in San Diego last month. “We’re like, bro, it’s never going to happen. What are you talking about? Where are you getting this information? Two years later, here we are.”
Growing without adding dispatchers
Spartan runs a 24/7 operation with four dispatchers: one on each shift and one who covers weekends and fills gaps. Dawson’s test for any new tool is how the carrier would double its volume without hiring another dispatcher.
“We don’t want to let anybody go, we don’t want to fire anyone. That’s not the point,” he said. “It’s how can I maximize my operation with the same headcount that I have now, and allow those people an opportunity to grow and learn to do different things.”
Dawson said many people get into logistics to solve problems, and dispatchers don’t always get the chance.
“I have a hard time believing that anybody goes into logistics because they want to look through PDF documents, or they want to look at a screen all day long and just press a button,” he said.
To teach someone a new skill, he said, he first has to free up their time.
Hourly reports became the first agent
A couple of Spartan’s customers want status updates in a set format every hour, on the hour. A dispatcher built each one by hand in Excel, which took seven to 10 minutes on average and up to 15 for a newer hire. If Spartan doubled its volume, Dawson said, the same report would take closer to 20 minutes. When he asked dispatchers in July which one task they would eliminate, every one of them named the hourly route updates.
Dawson met once with an Alvys staffer to learn Foundry and once more to hand off the report. A sample came back in about two days, and the agent was running within a week and a half. He had forgotten he switched it on until his inbox filled during the operations team’s 9:30 a.m. call.
“Literally 10 o’clock, 11 o’clock, 12 o’clock, 1 o’clock, perfectly on time,” he said.
The automated reports matched his dispatchers’ “almost 100%,” Dawson said, and he planned to start sending them to customers the following Monday. By his estimate, that one agent frees 17% of a dispatcher’s day.
“If I knock out two more that are similar in weight or capacity, I just gave them half of their day back,” he said.
The freed time also shows him what each dispatcher gravitates toward, he said, which helps him decide who takes on new projects, including Spartan’s work in Foundry.
From one truck to 150
Llanes bought one truck, then grew the fleet to five, 10, and 20 until it reached the 50 trucks Spartan’s first contract required, Dawson said. Spartan began hauling directly for Toyota in 2023 with 5% of one location’s freight. It now handles about 30% at one plant and 20% at another, he said, and is one of 12 motor carriers in North America that run directly for Toyota.
The carrier serves Toyota’s plants in San Antonio and Blue Springs, Mississippi, and works with a group at the Mazda Toyota Manufacturing plant in Huntsville, Alabama. The fleet stands at about 150 trucks, 400 trailers , and 170 drivers, Dawson said.
Driver payroll is the next test
Spartan pays drivers a flat weekly guarantee for working five days a week. Most of its freight moves on relays: a load from Detroit to San Antonio can pass through six solo drivers, with handoffs in Fort Wayne, Indiana; Shepherdsville, Kentucky; Memphis, Tennessee; Arkansas; and Dallas.
When one driver runs late, hours-of-service limits push that route later each day. Managers pull in on-call extra-board drivers to hold Toyota’s schedule, and drivers who lose a day through no fault of their own still have to be paid. Field teams sort that out by checking Samsara ELD logs and their own notes, which Dawson said usually takes an entire Monday.
“Driver workforce is the number one most important thing for any logistics company,” he said. “But in order for them to be happy, you can’t mess up their payroll.”
The workflow Spartan is building would email field teams each day with every driver missing from the dispatch planner and ask whether to log a call-off or an unplanned extra-board day. An approval would add the day to the planner and a line item to that driver’s settlement report. A weekly summary would list every decision.
It has not been tested yet, and Dawson expects it to cut payroll time at least in half.
Operators learning to build agents
Spartan moved to Alvys from a previous transportation management system that Dawson said was “not as innovation focused.” Alvys staff built Spartan’s first agent with Dawson. For payroll, he planned to start editing the Foundry workflows himself once he was back in the office, and he wants his dispatchers and field operators doing the same.
“I’m not a tech guy, I’m not a coder, I’m not a data scientist. I just run trucks,” he said.
The first template Alvys sent him needs only a customer name and a choice of report format, he said.
“If I got 25 customers tomorrow, I would just say, what template do you want, A, B, or C?” Dawson said.
Payroll is harder.
“So far, it seems relatively intuitive, but there’s some nuances that I think are a little bit difficult,” he said. Because of how intricate Spartan’s payroll is, he sees it as the real test. “If that one is easy, I cannot imagine the other ones being any more difficult. If I can get that one down, we’re going.”
Why it matters: Spartan’s first Foundry agent builds the hourly reports a four-person dispatch desk made by hand at a carrier that grew to 150 trucks in five years. It’s a growing example of fleet operators scaling through technology and automation compared to adding headcount in years past.
